docs.title: Type
docs.text:
Token Size / line-height Face, weight Use --fs-xs 12 / 16 Sans 500 Captions, date group headings, footnotes --fs-sm 13 / 18 Sans 400 Stats line, meta, table head --fs-md 14 / 20 Sans 400–600 Sidebar, buttons, table cells --fs-body 16 / 25 Sans 400 Question, notices, plan, composer --fs-claim 20 / 28 Serif 500 Claim headline --fs-display 28 / 34 Serif 500 Empty-state greeting

Weights 400/500/600 only. Sentence case everywhere (no tracked uppercase). Numbers in tables use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums.

docs.title: Space, radius, elevation
docs.text:
• Spacing: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 (--sp-1 … --sp-8). Nothing off this ladder.
  • Radii: 6 controls, 10 cards/tables/panels, 16 composer, full for chips.
  • Elevation: light uses --shadow-1 on the composer and --shadow-2 on menus/sheets; dark uses no shadows, only a lighter surface plus a 1 px border.
  • Layout: sidebar 264 px; chat column max 760 px with 24 px side padding; dataset panel 440 px sheet from the right. Under 1000 px wide the sidebar narrows to 232 px; the column stays fluid. Under 700 CSS px (the 800 × 600 minimum window at 200% zoom is 400 px wide) the sidebar folds behind a "Cohort and conversations" toggle (aria-expanded). The open drawer is not modal: its close button and Escape return focus to the toggle; a click outside it or focus moving out of it closes it; its scroll is contained. The language model banner can be dismissed so the composer stays on screen; the offline banner cannot, because its "Try again" is the only way to reconnect. The composer shows the same 2 px --focus-ring outline as every other control on :focus-within.

docs.title: Motion (after Kowalski)
docs.text:
Token Value --ease-out cubic-bezier(.23, 1, .32, 1) --ease-in-out cubic-bezier(.77, 0, .175, 1) --dur-press 100 ms --dur-hover 120 ms --dur-pop 180 ms --dur-enter 220 ms --dur-exit 140 ms --press-scale .97

Choreography: - Send: button presses to scale(.97) (transform only). The question bubble enters at once (opacity + 4 px rise, 180 ms). - Working: three dots pulse opacity on a 1.2 s cycle; the stage text ("Reading your question", "Running the analysis") is a sibling, static, and swaps text without moving. After 3 s an elapsed counter appears. - Answer lands: the card enters with opacity 0→1, translateY(6px)→0, blur(2px)→0 over 220 ms; caption, claim, stats and table stagger by 40–60 ms. Numbers never count up. - Held card: same entry. After "Run this analysis" the plan stays and the result arrives below; after "Not what I meant" the buttons are replaced by a one-line note. - Scroll: when the reader was at the bottom, a new answer is scrolled into view; if the answer is taller than the view, its top is aligned instead so the headline is never off-screen. - Hover effects are gated behind (hover: hover). Transitions name their properties (no transition: all). - Reduced motion: no translate, no blur, no pulse; opacity fades of 150 ms remain, scroll is instant.

docs.title: Message states
docs.text: State Shape Label / icon Copy Answered No box; caption, serif headline (an h3; the message is an article labelled by its question), stats line, what was computed, caveats, table, footnote Analysis type as caption Claim text from the API, unchanged; under it the plan from plan_line as a small list that always shows who was included ("Age over 83") and what was counted ("Rows" or "Patients (each Patient ID once)"). The footnote appears whenever anything is hidden, in the table or in the claim ("Total count hidden."). A table whose every value is hidden is not drawn; a table with more than 20 groups is never drawn ("The table isn’t shown because it has N groups…"). Table numbers use the claim's precision (p-values aside); "outcome=0" reads "Outcome: 0". The live region reads "Answer: {headline}". Held Tinted draft card with border Clock icon + "Check this plan before it runs" API reason, a next step (for words it couldn't place: "This cohort has LDL and HDL. If you meant one of them, choose “Not what I meant” and ask again using its name."), then the plan as a labelled list (a missing value reads "Not set"; internal flags are not shown), the exact plan text on demand, buttons "Run this analysis" / "Not what I meant" ("Not what I meant" is the primary button when words were left out) Confirmed Held card, buttons replaced "You approved this plan. The answer is below." Result streams below. If the answer below is a refusal or an error: "Not run — see below." Rejected Held card, buttons replaced "Not run." "Not run. Rephrase your question below." Refused Neutral notice Info icon + "Not answered" API reason, then "Your question is back in the box below so you can change it." Error Danger-tinted notice Alert icon + "Something went wrong" A plain sentence, never engine or exception text ("Execution error: …" is an error, not a refusal). A network failure: "Couldn’t reach the analysis engine. Ask again; if it keeps happening, restart the app." An HTTP 5xx: "The analysis engine ran into a problem with this question. Ask again in other words; if it keeps happening, restart the app." A 4xx keeps the server’s reason in plain words (a 404 for a deleted cohort: "This cohort no longer exists…"). Upload, delete and panel errors never mention "this question" The engine's exact words only behind "Copy details"; question restored Loading Dots + stage text — "Reading your question", "Running the analysis", "· 4 s" after 3 s Streaming Send becomes Stop; composer stays editable Stop icon Enter while busy: "Wait for this answer, or press Stop." Stopped Muted note "Stopped" "Stopped waiting for this answer.", shown the moment Stop is pressed, even before the question reached the engine (the request is aborted). After an approved plan, its card settles ("You approved this plan, then stopped waiting. Ask again to see an answer.") and is never offered again. Empty (no cohort) Centred — "Choose a cohort to begin." + Upload / Use the sample cohort Empty (cohort chosen) Centred serif greeting + chips — "What would you like to know about {cohort}?" + three questions built from its columns (fill the box, never auto-send) Offline Banner at the top of the main column; empty state explains Alert icon "Can't reach the analysis engine on this computer." + Try again; empty state "Waiting for the analysis engine." Deleting In-page dialog under the cohort switcher — Existing delete copy; "Deleting…" while busy

docs.title: Theme
docs.text:
• Three choices: System, Light, Dark, as a segmented radio group in the sidebar footer.
  • Electron: the renderer calls window.appTheme.set(source) (preload → ipcMain.handle), main sets nativeTheme.themeSource, which drives prefers-color-scheme in the page, and persists the choice to settings.json in the app's user-data folder. Main reads it before the window is created and sets the window backgroundColor to match, so the first frame is already the right theme. Only the app's own page may call it, and only these three values are accepted. Main also passes the saved choice to preload (--ca-theme=<source>), exposed as appTheme.initial, and the <head> script uses it first, so a stale localStorage copy can never paint the other theme.
  • Browser (Vite, Playwright): an inline script in <head> reads localStorage (wrapped in try) and sets data-theme before first paint; the stylesheet does the rest.
  • Theme change cross-fades background and text colours for 200 ms (none under reduced motion).

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
• Sidebar (top to bottom): app name; cohort switcher (native <select>, so keyboard and screen readers work as before) with a ⋯ button opening a small menu: Upload a file, Use the sample cohort, Preview and details, Refresh the list, Delete this cohort; a meta line "400 rows · 14 variables" (rows, not "patients": a file can hold several rows per patient, and the meta line must not claim what it has not checked); a "New question" button; past conversations grouped by Today / Yesterday / Previous 7 days / Older; footer with the on-this-computer status and the theme switch.
  • Main: the chat column and the docked composer only. An offline banner appears only when the engine cannot be reached; the "Backend connected" badge is gone.
  • Dataset panel: a sheet from the right with the preview table, variable suggestions and change history. Opened from the ⋯ menu or the meta line; Escape or the close button returns focus to where it came from.

docs.title: Copy deck
docs.text:
Plain clinical language; "cohort" for the uploaded dataset, "rows" for rows (the API's own claims say "patients" where it has counted patients), no internal ids on screen.

Where Before After Title Clinical Analytics + ◉ Clinical Analytics (text only) Status (connected) Backend connected Running on this computer Status (offline) Backend unavailable Can't reach the analysis engine on this computer. Bundled in electron/src/fonts/, unmodified, served from the app (no network at runtime).

File Source (primary) Version Licence SourceSans3VF-Upright.woff2 adobe-fonts/source-sans, branch release, WOFF2/VF/SourceSans3VF-Upright.ttf.woff2 3.3408 SIL OFL 1.1 SourceSans3VF-Italic.woff2 same repository, WOFF2/VF/SourceSans3VF-Italic.ttf.woff2 3.3408 SIL OFL 1.1 SourceSerif4VF-Roman.woff2 adobe-fonts/source-serif, branch release, WOFF2/VAR/SourceSerif4Variable-Roman.ttf.woff2 4.328 SIL OFL 1.1

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Session titles after a restart need the API to persist the first question (see above).
  • Earlier answers in a resumed session are not shown: the API has no transcript endpoint.
  • The confirm request is built in one function (buildConfirmRequest in electron/src/confirmHold.js) so a server-issued hold token can be added in one place.

docs.title: Module boundaries (as-built)
docs.text: Purpose: reduce guesswork when reviewing imports and ownership across api/, core/, ui/, and datasets/.

docs.title: Intended dependency direction
docs.text:
• clinical_analytics.core: Domain logic—semantic layer, NL query engine, overlays, query execution helpers, schemas. No FastAPI or Streamlit imports.
  • clinical_analytics.datasets: Dataset definitions and factories (including uploaded datasets). May use core types.
  • clinical_analytics.api: HTTP transport, Pydantic schemas, route handlers, small adapters. Should call into core and datasets for behavior.
  • clinical_analytics.ui: Streamlit pages and components. May call core and datasets directly (today’s Streamlit path).

docs.title: Known couplings (review hotspots)
docs.text:
These are real today; tightening them is a migration concern tracked in the omnibus spec.

From To Notes api/routes/datasets.py ui.storage.user_datasets.UserDatasetStorage Upload path shares storage with Streamlit. api/routes/enrichments.py ui.components.enrichment_integration.EnrichmentService Enrichment wiring crosses UI package.

Prefer new API-only code to live under api/services/ or core/ rather than adding more api → ui imports unless the omnibus explicitly keeps a temporary bridge.

docs.title: Duplicate names
docs.text: • QueryService: clinical_analytics.core.query_service (engine) vs clinical_analytics.api.services.query_service (async adapter). The API layer wraps core types (see api/services/query_service.py).

docs.title: NL Query → Semantic Layer
docs.text:
# Phase 3: Enhanced QuestionEngine
class QuestionEngine:
    @staticmethod
    def parse_natural_language_query(
        query: str,
        semantic_layer: SemanticLayer
    ) -> AnalysisIntent:
        # 1. Get semantic layer metadata
        config = semantic_layer.config

        # 2. Extract available entities
        outcomes = list(config.get('outcomes', {}).keys())
        variables = list(config.get('column_mapping', {}).values())

        # 3. Use embeddings to match query to entities
        matched_outcome = match_entity(query, outcomes)
        matched_variables = match_entities(query, variables)

        # 4. Infer intent
        intent = infer_intent_from_query(query)

        return AnalysisIntent(
            intent=intent,
            outcome=matched_outcome,
            variables=matched_variables
        )

docs.text:

docs.title: 3. Semantic Understanding
docs.text:

docs.text:

  • SemanticLayer: SQL generation
  • Registry: Dataset management

docs.title: 5. Boundary Rules
docs.text:
IO is eager, transforms are lazy, semantics are declarative.

  • IO Boundary: File reads (pl.read_csv(), pl.read_parquet()) are eager. Use pl.scan_csv()/pl.scan_parquet() for lazy IO when possible. DuckDB writes materialize data.
  • Transform Boundary: All data transformations use Polars lazy frames (pl.LazyFrame). Materialize only at query execution or UI render boundary.
  • Semantic Boundary: Semantic layer config is declarative (JSON/YAML). No imperative logic in semantic layer initialization.
  • Documentation: Any code that violates these boundaries must have explicit comment explaining why (e.g., Excel files require eager read due to Polars limitations).

Persistence Invariant: "Given the same upload hash + semantic config, results are immutable and reused."

This means: - Same content hash → same dataset_version → same DuckDB table → same query results - Query execution uses (upload_id, dataset_version) as idempotent run key - Semantic config changes create new version (different results)

docs.title: Architecture Refactoring: From Hardcoded to Config-Driven
docs.text:
Date: 2025-12-07 Status: ✅ Complete (Historical) Impact: Critical - Foundation for true extensibility

⚠️ Historical Document: This document describes the architectural refactoring that moved from hardcoded datasets to a registry pattern. The built-in datasets (COVID-MS, Sepsis, MIMIC-III) used as examples have been removed. The registry pattern now supports user-uploaded datasets only.

docs.title: 🎯 Objective
docs.text: Transform the Clinical Analytics Platform from a hardcoded, brittle system into a truly config-driven, extensible architecture that follows DRY principles and enables zero-code addition of new datasets.

docs.title: 1. Hardcoded Dataset Lists
docs.text:
# BEFORE: Hardcoded in UI
dataset_choice = st.sidebar.selectbox(
    "Choose Dataset",
    ["COVID-MS", "Sepsis", "MIMIC-III (Coming Soon)"]  # HARDCODED!
)

docs.title: 2. Manual Dataset Loading (if/else Hell)
docs.text:
# BEFORE: Manual if/else chain
if dataset_name == "COVID-MS":
    dataset = CovidMSDataset()
elif dataset_name == "Sepsis":
    dataset = SepsisDataset()
else:
    return None  # Fragile!

docs.title: 3. Hardcoded Column Mappings
docs.text:
# BEFORE: Hardcoded in each dataset
cohort = df.select([
    pl.col('secret_name').alias('patient_id'),  # HARDCODED!
    pl.col('age_in_cat').alias('age_group'),    # HARDCODED!
    pl.col('dmt_type_overall').alias('dmt'),    # HARDCODED!
])

docs.title: 4. No Centralized Configuration
docs.text:
• Column mappings scattered across dataset files
  • Default predictors hardcoded in UI logic
  • No single source of truth for dataset metadata

docs.title: 1. Dataset Registry with Auto-Discovery
docs.text:
File: src/clinical_analytics/core/registry.py

class DatasetRegistry:
    """Auto-discovers and manages all ClinicalDataset implementations"""

    @classmethod
    def discover_datasets(cls) -> Dict[str, Type[ClinicalDataset]]:
        """Scan datasets/ folder and auto-discover implementations"""
        # No hardcoding - uses reflection to find all ClinicalDataset subclasses

    @classmethod
    def get_dataset(cls, name: str, **params) -> ClinicalDataset:
        """Factory method - zero hardcoded if/else chains"""
        dataset_class = cls._datasets[name]
        return dataset_class(**params)

Benefits: - ✅ Add new dataset = drop file in datasets/ folder, done! - ✅ UI automatically picks it up - ✅ No code changes required

docs.title: 2. Centralized Configuration
docs.text:
File: data/configs/datasets.yaml

covid_ms:
  display_name: "COVID-19 & Multiple Sclerosis"
  status: "available"

  init_params:
    source_path: "data/raw/covid_ms/GDSI_OpenDataset_Final.csv"

  column_mapping:
    secret_name: patient_id        # Single source of truth!
    age_in_cat: age_group
    dmt_type_overall: dmt

  analysis:
    default_outcome: outcome_hospitalized
    default_predictors: [age_group, sex, dmt]
    categorical_variables: [age_group, sex]

  default_filters:
    confirmed_only: true

Benefits: - ✅ All dataset config in one place - ✅ Change mapping = edit YAML, not code - ✅ Non-developers can configure datasets - ✅ Version control for data transformations

class ColumnMapper:
    """Applies transformations based on config, not hardcoded logic"""

    def map_to_unified_cohort(self, df: pl.DataFrame, ...) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Generic mapping using config - works for ANY dataset"""

Benefits: - ✅ DRY - one mapping engine for all datasets - ✅ Consistent behavior across datasets - ✅ Easy to test and maintain

docs.text:
File: src/clinical_analytics/ui/app.py

# AFTER: Dynamic, config-driven

docs.title: 🚀 How to Add a New Dataset (Zero Hardcoding!)
Step 1: Create dataset module
docs.text:
mkdir -p src/clinical_analytics/datasets/my_dataset
touch src/clinical_analytics/datasets/my_dataset/__init__.py

docs.title: Step 2: Implement dataset class
docs.text:
# src/clinical_analytics/datasets/my_dataset/definition.py
from clinical_analytics.core.dataset import ClinicalDataset
from clinical_analytics.core.mapper import ColumnMapper, load_dataset_config

class MyDataset(ClinicalDataset):
    def __init__(self, source_path: Optional[str] = None):
        self.config = load_dataset_config('my_dataset')
        if source_path is None:
            source_path = self.config['init_params']['source_path']
        super().__init__(name="my_dataset", source_path=source_path)
        self.mapper = ColumnMapper(self.config)

    def validate(self) -> bool:
        return self.source_path.exists()

    def load(self) -> None:
        # Load your data...
        pass

    def get_cohort(self, **filters) -> pd.DataFrame:
        # Use mapper for transformation
        return self.mapper.map_to_unified_cohort(
            self._data,
            time_zero_value="...",
            outcome_col=self.mapper.get_default_outcome()
        ).to_pandas()

docs.title: Step 3: Add configuration
docs.text:
# data/configs/datasets.yaml
my_dataset:
  display_name: "My Dataset Name"
  status: "available"

  init_params:
    source_path: "data/raw/my_dataset/data.csv"

  column_mapping:
    my_patient_col: patient_id
    my_age_col: age

  analysis:
    default_outcome: my_outcome
    default_predictors: [age, gender]

docs.title: Step 4: Done!
docs.text:
• No code changes to UI
  • No hardcoded if/else statements
  • Dataset automatically appears in dropdown
  • All behavior driven by config

docs.title: 1. DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself)
docs.text:
• Single column mapping engine (not repeated per dataset)
  • Single registry pattern (not multiple discovery mechanisms)
  • Config defined once, used everywhere

docs.title: 2. Open/Closed Principle
docs.text:
• Open for extension: Add new datasets without modifying existing code
  • Closed for modification: Core system doesn't change when adding datasets

docs.title: 3. Dependency Inversion
docs.text:
• High-level modules (UI) depend on abstractions (Registry)
  • Not on concrete implementations (CovidMSDataset, SepsisDataset)

docs.title: 4. Single Responsibility
docs.text:
• Registry: Discovers and instantiates datasets
  • Mapper: Applies transformations
  • Datasets: Load data
  • UI: Displays data
  • Each component does ONE thing well

docs.title: 5. Configuration Over Code
docs.text:
• Business logic in YAML, not Python
  • Non-developers can configure datasets
  • Changes don't require deployment

docs.title: Code Quality
docs.text:
• Before: 200+ lines of hardcoded logic across files
  • After: <50 lines of config, reusable components
  • Reduction: ~75% less imperative code

docs.title: Maintainability
docs.text:
• Before: Touch 4+ files to add dataset
  • After: 1 file (YAML) + 1 implementation
  • Improvement: 75% fewer touchpoints

docs.title: Extensibility
docs.text:
• Before: Developer required to add dataset
  • After: Data scientist can add via config
  • Improvement: Zero-code dataset addition

docs.title: Test Coverage
docs.text:
• Before: Test each dataset individually
  • After: Test registry + mapper once, works for all
  • Improvement: O(1) vs O(n) test complexity

docs.title: 🔮 Future Enhancements Enabled
docs.text:
This refactoring enables:

  1. Plugin System: Load datasets from external packages
  2. Remote Configurations: Fetch dataset configs from API
  3. Multi-Tenancy: Different configs for different users
  4. Dataset Versioning: Track config changes in git
  5. Automated Testing: Config-driven test generation
  6. Documentation Generation: Auto-generate docs from config

docs.title: ✅ Acceptance Criteria Met
docs.text:
• [x] No hardcoded dataset lists
  • [x] No if/else chains for dataset loading
  • [x] No hardcoded column mappings
  • [x] Single source of truth for configuration
  • [x] Auto-discovery of datasets
  • [x] Dynamic UI population
  • [x] DRY principles applied
  • [x] Extensible without code changes
  • [x] All tests passing
  • [x] Config-driven transformations

docs.title: 🎉 Conclusion
docs.text:
The Clinical Analytics Platform is now a truly config-driven, extensible system. We've eliminated hardcoding, applied DRY principles, and enabled zero-code addition of new datasets.

This is not a demo - this is production-grade architecture.

Adding a new dataset now requires: 1. Implement dataset class (follows standard pattern) 2. Add configuration to YAML 3. Done!

No UI changes, no registry modifications, no hardcoded logic. The system auto-discovers and integrates new datasets seamlessly.

We built it right this time. 🚀

  ST --> UPL

Trust boundary: Local development assumes a trusted machine. FastAPI is bound for local use with CORS defaults suitable for dev; do not treat that as production hardening. See THREAT_MODEL.md.

docs.title: Data contracts: known limits
docs.text:
Each upload version gets one ODCS v3.2.0 contract in <data home>/data/contracts/<upload_id>/<version>.odcs.yaml, written once, and a quality report per run in dq/.

  • Version is not bumped on accepted patches. The contract is built from the metadata patches accepted when it is first written (listed in its metadataPatchIds). A patch accepted later does not produce a new contract or bump version (it stays 1.0.0). Re-contracting on patch acceptance is deferred; until then a contract can lag the resolved metadata.
  • Multi-table uploads get one contract for the combined table only.
  • Lab values get no plausibility range until units are captured.

make test-fast
make run-api   # API (another terminal)
make run       # Streamlit

GitHub Actions runs the Electron renderer Playwright job (electron-playwright in .github/workflows/ci.yml). Locally use make test-electron-e2e (after cd electron && npm ci) or cd electron && npm run test:e2e. This is Chromium + Vite, not the packaged Electron binary.

docs.title: Dataset Structure Patterns
docs.text:
Date: 2025-12-24 Purpose: Document the consistent file structure patterns across datasets

Note: This document describes file structure patterns using historical examples from PhysioNet datasets (COVID-MS, Sepsis, MIMIC). These built-in datasets have been removed from the platform code. The patterns documented here serve as reference examples for how user-uploaded datasets should be structured for optimal NL query support.

docs.title: 📁 Standard Dataset Structure
docs.text:
Clinical datasets from PhysioNet and similar sources follow a consistent structure that includes:

  1. Data Files - The actual dataset (CSV, PSV, or relational tables) in data/raw/
  2. README/Documentation - Data dictionary with column descriptions
  3. Original location: In data/raw/{dataset}/ alongside data files
  4. License Files - Usage terms and conditions
  5. Checksums - File integrity verification

Note: For how dictionaries are supplied today, see Data Dictionaries under Platform Integration.

docs.title: 🔍 COVID-MS Dataset Structure
docs.text:
Location: data/raw/covid_ms/

covid_ms/
├── GDSI_OpenDataset_Final.csv    # Main data file (1,141 patients)
├── README.txt                     # Data dictionary & description
├── LICENSE.txt                     # CC BY 4.0 License
└── SHA256SUMS.txt                 # File integrity checksums

docs.title: README.txt Contents
docs.text:
• Dataset description
  • Repository contents
  • Usage guidelines
  • License information
  • Data collection methodology

Example: 

Patient-level dataset to study the effect of COVID-19 in people with Multiple Sclerosis

Description:
This repository contains the anonymized open-sourced dataset from the
COVID-19 and Multiple Sclerosis (MS) Global Data Sharing Initiative (GDSI).
The dataset comprises data entered by people with MS and clinicians...

Repository Contents:
- 'GDSI_OpenDataset_Final.csv': The anonymized and de-identified dataset
  containing data collected from 1141 people with Multiple Sclerosis...

docs.title: 🔍 Sepsis Dataset Structure
docs.text:
Location: data/raw/sepsis/physionet.org/files/challenge-2019/1.0.0/

sepsis/
├── training/                       # Training data directory
│   ├── p000001.psv                # Patient data files (PSV format)
│   ├── p000002.psv
│   └── ...                        # Multiple PSV files (one per patient)
├── physionet_challenge_2019_ccm_manuscript.pdf  # Data dictionary & methodology
├── LICENSE.txt                     # CC BY 4.0 License
└── SHA256SUMS.txt                  # File integrity checksums

docs.title: Sepsis Documentation Structure
docs.text:
Unlike COVID-MS which uses README.txt, Sepsis uses a PDF manuscript:

  • physionet_challenge_2019_ccm_manuscript.pdf - Comprehensive documentation including:
  • Dataset description and methodology
  • Data collection process
  • Column/variable definitions
  • Data format specifications (PSV format)
  • Outcome definitions (SepsisLabel)
  • Feature descriptions (vital signs, lab values, etc.)
  • Usage guidelines and challenge details

Key Information in PDF: - Data Format: PSV (pipe-separated values) - Time Series: Hourly measurements per patient - Outcome: SepsisLabel (binary: 0/1) - Features: Age, Gender, vital signs, lab values, etc. - Aggregation: Time-series data aggregated to patient-level

Note: The PDF serves the same purpose as README.txt - it's the data dictionary and methodology documentation, just in PDF format instead of text.

docs.title: 🔍 MIMIC Dataset Structure
docs.text: MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV follow the same pattern:

docs.title: MIMIC-IV Demo Structure
docs.text:
mimic4_demo/
├── hosp/                          # Hospital module
│   ├── admissions.csv             # Admission records
│   ├── patients.csv               # Patient demographics
│   ├── diagnoses_icd.csv          # ICD diagnosis codes
│   ├── labevents.csv              # Laboratory results
│   └── ...
├── icu/                           # ICU module
│   ├── icustays.csv
│   ├── chartevents.csv
│   └── ...
├── README.md                      # Comprehensive data dictionary
├── LICENSE.txt                    # Usage license
└── documentation/                 # Additional documentation
    ├── MIMIC_IV_Data_Dictionary.pdf
    └── ...

docs.title: MIMIC README Contents
docs.text:
MIMIC README files include: - Table descriptions - What each table contains - Column definitions - Detailed field descriptions - Data types - Column types and formats - Relationships - Foreign key relationships between tables - Usage examples - Sample queries and workflows - Data collection methodology - How data was collected - Temporal relationships - How time is represented

Example MIMIC README structure: 

# MIMIC-IV Data Dictionary

## Table: admissions

| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| hadm_id | integer | Hospital admission ID |
| subject_id | integer | Patient identifier |
| admittime | timestamp | Admission time |
| dischtime | timestamp | Discharge time |
| ...

## Relationships
- admissions.subject_id → patients.subject_id
- admissions.hadm_id → diagnoses_icd.hadm_id

docs.title: 1. Automatic Configuration Generation
docs.text: The consistent structure enables: - Data dictionary parsing - Extract column descriptions from README - Schema inference - Understand data types and relationships - Semantic layer auto-config - Generate datasets.yaml entries from documentation

docs.title: 2. Semantic Understanding for NL Queries
docs.text: When implementing NL queries (Phase 3), the data dictionary provides: - Variable synonyms - "mortality" = "death" = "deceased" - Column descriptions - Understand what each field means - Relationships - Know which tables join together - Context for RAG - Use README content as knowledge base

docs.title: 3. Consistent User Experience
docs.text: Users working with different datasets see: - Same file structure - Same documentation format - Same data dictionary style - Familiar patterns across datasets

docs.title: Data Dictionaries
docs.text:
Data dictionaries are supplied by the user with their own upload (a PDF, Markdown or text file inside the ZIP, a standalone PDF uploaded alongside the data, or added later to an existing upload). Their extracted text is stored as doc_context in the upload's metadata in the per-user data home and stays local; the repo ships no dictionaries.

The PDF dictionaries for the removed built-in datasets (COVID-MS, Sepsis) were previously kept in data/dictionaries/; that folder has been removed and is git-ignored.

docs.title: Current Implementation
docs.text:
User Uploaded Datasets: - ✅ Data files uploaded via Streamlit UI (CSV, Excel, ZIP) - ✅ Automatic schema inference detects patient ID, outcomes, time columns - ✅ Semantic layer config auto-generated from inferred schema - ✅ Data dictionaries can be included in ZIP uploads for RAG context

Reference Data Dictionaries: - The original PhysioNet project pages (COVID-MS, Sepsis) remain good examples of comprehensive documentation

docs.title: Future Enhancement: Auto-Parsing
docs.text:
Goal: Automatically generate semantic layer config from data dictionaries

# Future: Auto-generate config from a user-supplied data dictionary

def parse_data_dictionary(dict_path: str) -> dict:
    """
    Parse data dictionary to extract:
    - Table/column descriptions
    - Data types
    - Relationships
    - Outcome definitions

    Supports:
    - README.md or README.txt (text/markdown)
    - PDF files (supplied with the user's upload)
    """
    if dict_path.endswith('.pdf'):
        return parse_pdf_dictionary(dict_path)
    elif dict_path.endswith(('.txt', '.md')):
        return parse_text_dictionary(dict_path)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported dictionary format: {dict_path}")

# Example usage with a user-supplied dictionary
my_dict = parse_data_dictionary("my_dictionary.pdf")

Benefits: - Zero-code dataset addition (already achieved) - Zero-config dataset addition (future) - Automatic variable name mapping - Relationship inference from documentation

docs.title: 📊 Comparison: COVID-MS vs. Sepsis vs. MIMIC
docs.text:
Aspect COVID-MS Sepsis MIMIC Data Format Single CSV Multiple PSV files (time-series) Multiple relational CSVs Documentation README.txt PDF manuscript README.md + PDF Structure Flat table Time-series → aggregated Normalized relational Data Dictionary In README.txt In PDF manuscript Comprehensive in README.md License CC BY 4.0 CC BY 4.0 (PhysioNet) PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Checksums SHA256SUMS.txt SHA256SUMS.txt Included in distribution

Common Patterns: - ✅ All include documentation with data dictionary (README.txt, PDF, or README.md) - ✅ All include license files - ✅ All include file integrity checksums (SHA256SUMS.txt) - ✅ All document column meanings and data types - ✅ All provide usage guidelines - ✅ All follow PhysioNet distribution patterns

docs.title: 🎯 For NL Query Implementation
docs.text: When implementing semantic NL queries (Phase 3), the data dictionary becomes critical:

docs.title: 1. Entity Extraction
docs.text:
# Use documentation to understand variable names
# Dictionaries are supplied by the user with their upload (none ship in the repo)

# For COVID-MS: README.txt from raw data
data_dictionary = parse_readme("data/raw/covid_ms/README.txt")

# For Sepsis: the PDF the user uploaded with the data
data_dictionary = parse_pdf("my_sepsis_dictionary.pdf")

# For MIMIC: README.md (when available)
data_dictionary = parse_readme("data/raw/mimic4_demo/README.md")
# Or a PDF the user uploaded with the data

# User query: "What's the mortality rate?"
# Match "mortality" to:
# - Documentation description: "death" → deathtime column
# - Documentation description: "mortality" → dod (date of death) column
# - Sepsis: "sepsis" → SepsisLabel column

docs.title: 2. RAG Context
docs.text:
# Use documentation content as RAG knowledge base
# Works with README.txt, PDF, or README.md

semantic_context = {
    'data_dictionary': documentation_content,  # From README/PDF
    'table_descriptions': extract_table_descriptions(doc),
    'column_meanings': extract_column_descriptions(doc),
    'relationships': extract_relationships(doc),
    'outcome_definitions': extract_outcome_definitions(doc)  # SepsisLabel, mortality, etc.
}

# LLM uses this context to understand user queries
# Works across all dataset types (CSV, PSV, relational)

docs.title: 3. Synonym Mapping
docs.text:
# Extract synonyms from README descriptions
# "mortality" → ["death", "deceased", "died", "fatal"]
# "admission" → ["hospitalization", "stay", "encounter"]

docs.title: Recommended Documentation Structure
docs.text:
For consistency, dataset documentation (README.txt, README.md, or PDF) should include:

  1. Dataset Overview
  2. Description
  3. Source

  4. Collection methodology

  5. Data Dictionary

  6. Table/column descriptions
  7. Data types
  8. Value ranges/domains

  9. Outcome definitions

  10. Relationships (for relational data)

  11. Foreign keys
  12. Join patterns

  13. Temporal relationships

  14. Usage Guidelines

  15. How to load data
  16. Common queries
  17. Analysis examples

  18. Data format specifications (CSV, PSV, etc.)

  19. License & Citation

  20. License terms
  21. Citation requirements
  22. Attribution

Note: Format can vary (text, markdown, PDF) but content should cover these areas.

docs.title: ✅ Checklist for New Datasets
docs.text:
When adding a new dataset, ensure it includes:

  • [ ] Data files (CSV/PSV/relational)
  • [ ] Documentation with data dictionary (README.txt, README.md, or PDF)
  • [ ] License file
  • [ ] File integrity checksums (optional but recommended)
  • [ ] Column/variable descriptions
  • [ ] Data type documentation
  • [ ] Outcome definitions
  • [ ] Relationship documentation (for relational data)
  • [ ] Usage guidelines

Documentation Format Examples: - COVID-MS: README.txt (text file) - Sepsis: PDF manuscript (comprehensive documentation) - MIMIC: README.md + PDF (markdown + detailed PDF)

This consistent structure enables the platform to automatically understand and integrate new datasets, supporting both current config-driven architecture and future NL query capabilities.

docs.title: Ibis Semantic Layer - Config-Driven Architecture
docs.text: Status: ✅ Implemented Date: 2025-01-XX Principle: DRY, Config-Driven, Extensible

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text: The platform now uses Ibis to generate SQL dynamically behind the scenes, replacing the brittle custom Python mapping logic. Everything is driven by datasets.yaml configuration - no hardcoded logic.

docs.text:
• ✅ Auto-discovery via DatasetRegistry
  • ✅ No hardcoded dataset lists in UI

docs.title: 2. Column Mappings
docs.text:
• ✅ All column renames in column_mapping section
  • ✅ No hardcoded pl.col().alias() logic
  • ✅ Semantic layer reads config and builds SQL

docs.title: 3. Outcome Definitions
docs.text:
• ✅ Binary mappings (yes/no → 1/0) in outcomes section
  • ✅ CASE WHEN expressions generated from config
  • ✅ Multiple outcomes per dataset supported

docs.title: 4. Filters
docs.text:

docs.title: 🔧 How to Add a New Dataset
Step 1: Add Config Entry
docs.text:
# data/configs/datasets.yaml
my_new_dataset:
  name: "My Dataset"
  display_name: "My New Dataset"
  description: "Description here"
  source: "Source name"
  status: "available"

  init_params:
    source_path: "data/raw/my_dataset/data.csv"

  time_zero:
    value: "2020-01-01"

  column_mapping:
    id: patient_id
    age: age
    outcome_col: outcome

  outcomes:
    outcome:
      source_column: outcome_col
      type: binary
      mapping:
        yes: 1
        no: 0

  metrics:
    outcome_rate:
      expression: "outcome.mean()"
      type: "rate"
      label: "Outcome Rate"

  dimensions:
    age:
      label: "Age"
      type: "continuous"

  filters:
    active_only:
      type: equals
      column: status
      description: "Active patients only"

  default_filters:
    active_only: true

  analysis:
    default_outcome: outcome
    default_predictors:
      - age

docs.title: Step 2: Implement Dataset Class
docs.text:
# src/clinical_analytics/datasets/my_dataset/definition.py
from clinical_analytics.core.dataset import ClinicalDataset
from clinical_analytics.core.semantic import SemanticLayer
from clinical_analytics.core.mapper import load_dataset_config

class MyDataset(ClinicalDataset):
    def __init__(self, source_path=None):
        self.config = load_dataset_config('my_new_dataset')
        if source_path is None:
            source_path = self.config['init_params']['source_path']
        super().__init__(name="my_new_dataset", source_path=source_path)
        self.semantic = SemanticLayer('my_new_dataset', config=self.config)

    def validate(self) -> bool:
        return self.source_path.exists() if self.source_path else False

    def load(self) -> None:
        if not self.validate():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Source not found: {self.source_path}")
        print(f"Semantic layer initialized for {self.name}")

    def get_cohort(self, **filters) -> pd.DataFrame:
        outcome_col = filters.get("target_outcome")
        filter_only = {k: v for k, v in filters.items() if k != "target_outcome"}
        return self.semantic.get_cohort(
            outcome_col=outcome_col,
            filters=filter_only
        )

docs.title: Step 3: Register in __init__.py
docs.text:
# src/clinical_analytics/datasets/__init__.py
from .my_dataset.definition import MyDataset

That's it! The registry auto-discovers it, UI shows it, query builder works.

docs.title: 🔍 Query Builder Usage
docs.text:
The query builder is fully config-driven:

  1. Metrics come from metrics section in config
  2. Dimensions come from dimensions section in config
  3. Filters come from filters section in config
  4. SQL is generated behind the scenes via Ibis

docs.title: Example Query
docs.text:
User selects: - Metrics: hospitalization_rate, patient_count - Dimensions: age_group, sex - Filters: confirmed_only = true

Generated SQL (behind the scenes): 

SELECT
  age_group,
  sex,
  AVG(outcome_hospitalized) as "Hospitalization Rate",
  COUNT(*) as "Patient Count"
FROM covid_ms_raw
WHERE covid19_confirmed_case = 'confirmed'
GROUP BY age_group, sex

  3. No code duplication - transformations defined once in config
  4. Extensible - add new datasets/metrics/filters via config only

docs.title: Internal Models (Database)
docs.text:
from sqlalchemy import Column, String, Integer, DateTime, Float, Text, ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship

Base = declarative_base()

class Session(Base):
    """Database model for conversation sessions."""
    __tablename__ = "sessions"

    session_id = Column(String(50), primary_key=True)
    dataset_id = Column(String(100), nullable=False)
    created_at = Column(DateTime, nullable=False)
    updated_at = Column(DateTime, nullable=False)
    metadata = Column(Text, nullable=True)  # JSON

    messages = relationship("Message", back_populates="session", cascade="all, delete-orphan")

class Message(Base):
    """Database model for conversation messages."""
    __tablename__ = "messages"

    message_id = Column(String(50), primary_key=True)
    session_id = Column(String(50), ForeignKey("sessions.session_id"), nullable=False)
    role = Column(String(20), nullable=False)  # "user" or "assistant"
    content = Column(Text, nullable=False)
    run_key = Column(String(100), nullable=True)
    status = Column(String(20), nullable=False)  # "pending", "completed", "error"
    confidence = Column(Float, nullable=True)
    intent = Column(String(50), nullable=True)
    created_at = Column(DateTime, nullable=False)

    session = relationship("Session", back_populates="messages")

class CachedResult(Base):
    """Database model for cached query results."""
    __tablename__ = "cached_results"

    cache_id = Column(String(50), primary_key=True)
    session_id = Column(String(50), ForeignKey("sessions.session_id"), nullable=False)
    query_hash = Column(String(64), nullable=False, index=True)  # SHA256 hash
    result_data = Column(Text, nullable=False)  # JSON
    created_at = Column(DateTime, nullable=False)
    ttl_seconds = Column(Integer, nullable=False, default=3600)  # 1 hour default

docs.title: Server-Side Sessions
docs.text:
All conversation state is stored server-side in the database:

  1. Session Creation: When user starts conversation, POST /api/sessions creates session record
  2. Message Persistence: Each query/response is stored as a Message record
  3. Result Caching: Analysis results cached by query_hash for fast retrieval
  4. LRU Eviction: ResultCache service manages LRU eviction (max 5 results per session)
  5. Session Cleanup: Inactive sessions deleted after 30 days

State Lifecycle: 

User → Create Session → Execute Query → Store Message → Cache Result
                                        ↓
                              Update Session.updated_at
                                        ↓
                              [If cache full] → LRU Evict Oldest

      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify(queryRequest)
    }).then(r => r.json()),

    };
  }
});

docs.title: Query Execution Flow
docs.text:
1. User enters query in ChatInterface
   ↓
2. Frontend sends POST /api/queries
   ↓
3. FastAPI route validates request (Pydantic)
   ↓
4. QueryService.execute_query() called
   ↓
5. QuestionEngine.parse_query() extracts intent
   ↓
6. Check ResultCache for cached result (by query_hash)
   ↓
7a. [Cache hit] → Return cached result immediately
7b. [Cache miss] → Execute via SemanticLayer
   ↓
8. SemanticLayer generates SQL via Ibis
   ↓
9. DuckDB executes query
   ↓
10. ResultInterpreter generates plain-English explanation
   ↓
11. Store result in ResultCache (LRU eviction if needed)
   ↓
12. Stream result back to frontend via SSE
   ↓
13. Frontend renders result with appropriate renderer

docs.title: Semantic Layer FastAPI Adapter Patterns
docs.text:
Status: Phase 1.5 Complete - Patterns Documented Date: 2026-01-03 Related: LIGHTWEIGHT_UI_ARCHITECTURE.md

Update (2026-11): the unbounded _semantic_layer_cache dict and get_semantic_layer() below were replaced by a bounded, reference-counted cache (api/layer_cache.py). Routes take a lease (lease_semantic_layer()); the worker thread that uses the layer releases it when it is done with it. A layer is closed on a background thread only once it has left the cache and no lease is left, and its query core goes with it. semantic_layer_cache_size and the total duckdb_memory_budget are set in nl_query.yaml. The code samples below show the original design.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document describes the adapter patterns needed to use the existing SemanticLayer (DuckDB + Ibis) with FastAPI's async dependency injection system. These patterns replace Streamlit's @st.cache_resource pattern.

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text:
The existing SemanticLayer has these characteristics: - Non-picklable: Contains DuckDB connections and Ibis expressions that cannot be pickled - Singleton pattern: In Streamlit, cached with @st.cache_resource (one instance per dataset) - Synchronous: Current implementation is sync, but FastAPI routes are async - Stateful: Maintains DuckDB connection pool and query cache

FastAPI requirements: - Async-first: Routes are async by default - Dependency injection: Uses Depends() pattern, not decorators - Thread-safe: Must handle concurrent requests safely - No pickling required: Unlike Streamlit's @st.cache_data, Depends() doesn't require pickling

docs.title: Pattern 1: Singleton Dependency
docs.text:
Streamlit Pattern (OLD): 

@st.cache_resource(show_spinner="Loading semantic layer...")
def get_cached_semantic_layer(dataset_version: str, _dataset):
    """
    Get semantic layer with caching.

    Uses @st.cache_resource (not @st.cache_data) because:
    - SemanticLayer contains non-picklable objects (DuckDB/Ibis)
    - cache_resource stores objects in memory without serialization
    """
    return _dataset.get_semantic_layer()

FastAPI Pattern (NEW): 

# Module-level cache (singleton per dataset)
_semantic_layer_cache: dict[str, SemanticLayer] = {}

def get_semantic_layer(
    dataset_id: str = Path(..., description="Dataset ID")
) -> SemanticLayer:
    """
    FastAPI dependency that provides cached semantic layer instance.

    Replaces @st.cache_resource pattern:
    - Single instance per dataset_id
    - Stored in module-level dict (no pickling required)
    - Reused across all requests for same dataset
    - Not pickled (DuckDB connections are not picklable)

    Args:
        dataset_id: Dataset identifier for cache key

    Returns:
        SemanticLayer instance (cached)
    """
    if dataset_id not in _semantic_layer_cache:
        dataset = UploadedDatasetFactory.create_dataset(dataset_id)
        dataset.load()
        _semantic_layer_cache[dataset_id] = dataset.get_semantic_layer()

    return _semantic_layer_cache[dataset_id]


# Usage in route
@app.get("/api/datasets/{dataset_id}/info")
async def get_dataset_info(
    semantic_layer: Annotated[SemanticLayer, Depends(get_semantic_layer)]
):
    """Route using semantic layer dependency."""
    return semantic_layer.get_dataset_info()

Key differences: - ✅ No decorator: Dependency function, not decorator - ✅ Explicit cache key: dataset_id parameter - ✅ Module-level cache: Dict instead of Streamlit's internal cache - ✅ Type-safe: Full type hints with Annotated

docs.title: Pattern 2: Async Wrapper for Sync Operations
docs.text:
Problem: SemanticLayer's query() method is synchronous and may block the event loop during long-running queries.

Solution: Run queries in thread executor to avoid blocking.

import asyncio
from functools import wraps

def run_in_executor(func):
    """
    Decorator to run sync function in executor (non-blocking).

    Prevents long-running sync operations from blocking async event loop.
    """
    @wraps(func)
    async def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
        return await loop.run_in_executor(None, lambda: func(*args, **kwargs))
    return wrapper


# Usage in route
@app.post("/api/queries")
async def execute_query(
    request: QueryRequest,
    semantic_layer: Annotated[SemanticLayer, Depends(get_semantic_layer)]
):
    """Execute query asynchronously."""

    # Run query in executor to avoid blocking
    loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
    result = await loop.run_in_executor(
        None,
        semantic_layer.query,
        request.metrics,
        request.dimensions,
        request.filters,
    )

    return {"result": result.to_dict(orient="records")}

Alternative: If queries are very long-running, use background tasks:

from fastapi import BackgroundTasks

@app.post("/api/queries")
async def execute_query_background(
    request: QueryRequest,
    background_tasks: BackgroundTasks,
    semantic_layer: Annotated[SemanticLayer, Depends(get_semantic_layer)]
):
    """Execute query in background, stream results via SSE."""
    query_id = generate_query_id()

    def run_query():
        result = semantic_layer.query(
            request.metrics,
            request.dimensions,
            request.filters,
        )
        # Store result in cache for retrieval
        store_query_result(query_id, result)

    background_tasks.add_task(run_query)

    return {
        "query_id": query_id,
        "status": "processing",
        "stream_url": f"/api/queries/{query_id}/stream"
    }

docs.title: Pattern 3: DuckDB Connection Management
docs.text:
Problem: DuckDB connections need to be thread-safe for concurrent requests.

Solution: DuckDB's default configuration is thread-safe. Verify with tests.

# Test concurrent access (from test_semantic_layer_fastapi_compat.py)
def test_unit_semanticLayer_concurrent_noRaceConditions(app):
    """Verify concurrent requests don't cause DuckDB issues."""
    client = TestClient(app)

    with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=5) as executor:
        futures = [
            executor.submit(lambda: client.get("/test-query"))
            for _ in range(10)
        ]
        responses = [f.result() for f in futures]

    # All requests should succeed
    assert all(r.status_code == 200 for r in responses)

Configuration: 

# No special configuration needed for DuckDB
# Default settings are thread-safe
semantic_layer = SemanticLayer(
    dataset_name=name,
    cohort=cohort,
    config=config,
)
# DuckDB connection pool handles concurrent access automatically

docs.title: Pattern 4: Dependency Injection with Multiple Dependencies
docs.text:
Pattern: Combine semantic layer with other dependencies (user auth, session, etc.).

from fastapi import Depends, Header

def get_current_session(session_id: str = Header(...)) -> Session:
    """Get current session from header."""
    return SessionManager.get_session(session_id)

def get_semantic_layer_for_session(
    session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_current_session)]
) -> SemanticLayer:
    """Get semantic layer for current session's dataset."""
    return get_semantic_layer(session.dataset_id)


@app.post("/api/queries")
async def execute_query(
    request: QueryRequest,
    session: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_current_session)],
    semantic_layer: Annotated[SemanticLayer, Depends(get_semantic_layer_for_session)]
):
    """Route with multiple dependencies."""
    # Both session and semantic_layer available
    result = await run_query(semantic_layer, request)
    return result

docs.title: Pattern 5: Cache Invalidation
docs.text:
Problem: When dataset is updated, semantic layer cache needs to be invalidated.

Solution: Explicit cache invalidation on dataset updates.

def invalidate_semantic_layer_cache(dataset_id: str):
    """
    Invalidate semantic layer cache for a dataset.

    Call this when:
    - Dataset is deleted
    - Dataset is updated (new upload)
    - Dataset configuration changes
    """
    if dataset_id in _semantic_layer_cache:
        del _semantic_layer_cache[dataset_id]


@app.delete("/api/datasets/{dataset_id}")
async def delete_dataset(dataset_id: str):
    """Delete dataset and invalidate cache."""
    # Delete from storage
    UploadedDatasetFactory.delete_dataset(dataset_id)

    # Invalidate cache
    invalidate_semantic_layer_cache(dataset_id)

    return {"status": "deleted"}


@app.post("/api/datasets/{dataset_id}/refresh")
async def refresh_dataset(dataset_id: str):
    """Refresh dataset and invalidate cache."""
    # Reload dataset
    dataset = UploadedDatasetFactory.create_dataset(dataset_id)
    dataset.load()

    # Invalidate cache to force recreation
    invalidate_semantic_layer_cache(dataset_id)

    return {"status": "refreshed"}

docs.title: Migration Checklist
docs.text:
When migrating from Streamlit to FastAPI:

  • [x] Replace @st.cache_resource with module-level cache dict
  • [x] Use Depends() for dependency injection
  • [x] Run sync queries in loop.run_in_executor() for long operations
  • [x] Test concurrent access to verify thread-safety
  • [x] Implement cache invalidation on dataset updates
  • [x] Add type hints with Annotated[SemanticLayer, Depends(...)]
  • [ ] Monitor DuckDB connection pool usage in production
  • [ ] Add metrics for semantic layer cache hits/misses

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
1. Memory Usage: Module-level cache keeps all semantic layers in memory
  2. Mitigation: Implement LRU eviction if memory becomes an issue

  3. Production: Use Redis for distributed cache

  4. Cold Start: First request per dataset is slow (semantic layer creation)

  5. Mitigation: Pre-warm cache on application startup for common datasets

  6. Cache Invalidation: Manual invalidation required on dataset changes

  7. Mitigation: Document when to call invalidate_semantic_layer_cache()

docs.title: Semantic Layer Creation (One-time per dataset)
docs.text:
• Time: ~100-500ms depending on dataset size
  • Happens: Once per dataset per application restart
  • Cached: Yes (module-level singleton)

docs.title: Query Execution (Per request)
docs.text:
• Time: ~50-2000ms depending on query complexity
  • Happens: Every query request
  • Optimizations:
  • Run in executor for >100ms queries
  • Use background tasks for >1s queries
  • Stream results via SSE for long-running operations

docs.title: Concurrent Request Handling
docs.text:
• DuckDB: Thread-safe by default
  • Connection pool: Managed automatically
  • Max concurrent: Limited by available memory, not connections

docs.title: Recommendations
docs.text:
1. For simple queries (<100ms): Direct execution is fine 

    result = semantic_layer.query(...)

  2. For moderate queries (100ms-1s): Use executor 

    result = await loop.run_in_executor(None, semantic_layer.query, ...)

  3. For long queries (>1s): Use background task + SSE streaming 

    background_tasks.add_task(run_query_and_stream)

  4. Cache strategy: Module-level for MVP, Redis for production

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• FastAPI Dependency Injection
  • FastAPI Background Tasks
  • DuckDB Thread Safety
  • Streamlit Caching

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Dataset Registry is the central component for managing clinical datasets. It provides:

  1. Automatic schema inference from uploaded files
  2. Unified interface for user-uploaded datasets
  3. Multi-table support with automatic relationship detection
  4. Config-driven semantic layer integration

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[CSV/Excel/ZIP Upload] --> B[SchemaInferenceEngine]
    B --> C[InferredSchema]
    C --> D[Dataset Config]
    D --> E[DatasetRegistry]
    E --> F[SemanticLayer]

    G[Uploaded Datasets] --> D
    H[Multi-Table Handler] --> C

docs.title: SchemaInferenceEngine
docs.text:
Automatically detects:

  • Patient ID column (unique identifier)
  • Outcome columns (binary variables with outcome-related names)
  • Time columns (dates, survival time)
  • Event columns (binary indicators)
  • Categorical vs continuous variables

Detection Methods:

  1. Name-based heuristics: Pattern matching on column names
  2. Type analysis: Data type and uniqueness checks
  3. Statistical properties: Cardinality, missing values

docs.title: InferredSchema
docs.text:
Data class containing all detected schema elements:

@dataclass
class InferredSchema:
    patient_id_column: Optional[str]
    time_zero: Optional[str]
    outcome_columns: List[str]
    time_columns: List[str]
    event_columns: List[str]
    categorical_columns: List[str]
    continuous_columns: List[str]

docs.title: DatasetRegistry
docs.text:
Central registry managing all datasets:

class DatasetRegistry:
    @classmethod
    def register_from_dataframe(cls, dataset_name, df):
        # Infer schema
        schema = SchemaInferenceEngine.infer_schema(df)

        # Create config
        config = schema.to_dataset_config()

        # Register
        cls._registry[dataset_name] = {
            'class': AutoInferredDataset,
            'config': config,
            'df': df
        }

docs.title: MultiTableHandler
docs.text:
For complex datasets with multiple tables (e.g., MIMIC-IV):

  1. Load all CSVs from ZIP file
  2. Detect primary keys in each table
  3. Detect foreign key relationships
  4. Build join graph
  5. Execute joins to create unified cohort

docs.title: Registration Workflow
docs.text: Unified Architecture: Single-table and multi-table uploads use identical workflows. Single-table = multi-table with 1 table.

docs.title: Single Table Upload
docs.text:
1. User uploads CSV/Excel/SPSS
   ↓
2. normalize_upload_to_table_list() normalizes to table list
   ↓
3. SchemaInferenceEngine analyzes structure
   ↓
4. InferredSchema generated
   ↓
5. Dataset version computed (content hash)
   ↓
6. Saved to persistent DuckDB + Parquet export
   ↓
7. Individual table saved to {upload_id}_tables/
   ↓
8. Converted to Dataset Config
   ↓
9. Registered in DatasetRegistry
   ↓
10. SemanticLayer initialized (all tables registered in DuckDB)
   ↓
11. Ready for analysis

docs.title: Multi-Table Upload
docs.text:
1. User uploads ZIP with multiple CSVs
   ↓
2. normalize_upload_to_table_list() extracts all tables
   ↓
3. MultiTableHandler detects relationships
   ↓
4. Perform automatic joins (creates unified cohort)
   ↓
5. SchemaInferenceEngine analyzes structure
   ↓
6. InferredSchema generated
   ↓
7. Dataset version computed (content hash)
   ↓
8. Saved to persistent DuckDB + Parquet export
   ↓
9. All individual tables saved to {upload_id}_tables/
   ↓
10. Converted to Dataset Config
   ↓
11. Registered in DatasetRegistry
   ↓
12. SemanticLayer initialized (all tables registered in DuckDB)
   ↓
13. Ready for analysis

Key Differences: None. Both upload types follow identical workflow after normalization step.

docs.title: Auto-Inferred Config
docs.text:
Unified Format: Both single-table and multi-table uploads use inferred_schema format (not variable_mapping).

name: my_dataset
display_name: My Clinical Study
status: auto-inferred
upload_id: user_upload_20250101_120000_abc123
dataset_version: a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h8  # Content hash

column_mapping:
  patient_id: patient_id

outcomes:
  mortality:
    source_column: mortality
    type: binary
  readmission:
    source_column: readmission_30d
    type: binary

time_zero:
  source_column: admission_date

tables:  # All upload types have this (single-table = [table_0])
  - name: table_0  # Single-table uses filename stem
  - name: patients  # Multi-table uses ZIP entry names
  - name: admissions
    primary_key: patient_id
    foreign_key: patient_id
    relationship: one-to-many

granularities:  # Inferred from columns
  - patient_level
  - admission_level  # If admission_id column exists

Persistence: Metadata stored in data/uploads/metadata/{upload_id}.json with complete schema information.

docs.title: Schema Override
docs.text:
Users can manually override auto-detected schema:

from clinical_analytics.core.registry import DatasetRegistry

# Override patient ID
config = {
    'column_mapping': {'subject_id': 'patient_id'},
    'outcomes': {'death_28day': {'type': 'binary'}}
}

DatasetRegistry.update_config('my_dataset', config)

docs.title: Dataset Support
docs.text:
The platform supports user-uploaded datasets only. Built-in datasets (COVID-MS, Sepsis, MIMIC-III) have been removed in favor of a self-service upload model with automatic schema inference.

All datasets are now registered dynamically through the upload workflow with auto-inferred configurations.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The NL Query Engine transforms free-form text questions into structured query intents that the semantic layer can execute. It uses a three-tier architecture for robust parsing.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[User Query Text] --> B[Tier 1: Pattern Matching]
    B -->|Match| C[QueryIntent]
    B -->|No Match| D[Tier 2: Semantic Embeddings]
    D -->|Confidence > 75%| C
    D -->|Low Confidence| E[Tier 3: LLM Fallback]
    E --> C
    C --> F[Variable Extraction]
    F --> G[Semantic Layer]

docs.title: Tier 1: Pattern Matching
docs.text:
Fast regex-based matching for common query patterns.

Patterns:

# Group comparison
r"compare\s+(\w+)\s+(?:by|between|across)\s+(\w+)"

# Risk prediction
r"(?:what predicts|predictors of|predict)\s+(\w+)"

# Survival analysis
r"\b(survival|time to event|kaplan|cox)\b"

# Correlation
r"\b(correlat|relationship|associat)\b"

# Descriptive
r"\b(describe|summary|overview|statistics)\b"

Confidence: 90-95% (high certainty for exact matches)

Latency: <1ms

docs.title: Tier 2: Semantic Embeddings
docs.text:
Uses sentence-transformers to match query with template library.

Model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (local, no API calls)

Process:

  1. Encode user query to embedding vector
  2. Compute cosine similarity with all template embeddings
  3. Return best match if similarity > 0.70
  4. Extract variables from query using fuzzy matching

Confidence: Similarity score (0.70-1.0)

Latency: ~50ms

Privacy: Fully local, no data leaves your machine

docs.title: Tier 3: LLM Fallback
docs.text:
For complex or ambiguous queries, uses structured prompts with RAG.

Context Provided:

  • Available columns from semantic layer
  • Outcome definitions
  • Example queries
  • Variable synonyms

Request Format:

{
    "intent_type": str,  # DESCRIBE, COMPARE_GROUPS, etc.
    "primary_variable": str,
    "grouping_variable": str,
    "confidence": float
}

Confidence: Model-generated (0.3-0.9)

Latency: ~2-5s (API call)

Privacy: Only anonymized metadata sent (column names, types)

docs.title: QueryIntent Structure
docs.text:
@dataclass
class QueryIntent:
    intent_type: str  # Analysis type
    primary_variable: Optional[str]
    grouping_variable: Optional[str]
    predictor_variables: List[str]
    time_variable: Optional[str]
    event_variable: Optional[str]
    filters: Dict[str, Any]
    confidence: float  # 0.0-1.0

docs.title: DESCRIBE
docs.text:
Descriptive statistics for all variables.

Triggers:

  • "describe", "summary", "overview", "statistics"

Variables Extracted: None (uses all columns)

docs.title: COMPARE_GROUPS
docs.text:
Compare outcome between groups.

Triggers:

  • "compare X by Y"
  • "difference in X between Y"

Variables Extracted:

  • primary_variable: Outcome to compare
  • grouping_variable: Grouping variable

docs.title: FIND_PREDICTORS
docs.text:
Identify risk factors for an outcome.

Triggers:

  • "what predicts X"
  • "risk factors for X"
  • "predictors of X"

Variables Extracted:

  • primary_variable: Outcome to predict
  • predictor_variables: Covariates (default: all available)

docs.title: SURVIVAL
docs.text:
Survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier, Cox).

Triggers:

  • "survival", "time to event", "kaplan-meier"

Variables Extracted:

  • time_variable: Follow-up time
  • event_variable: Event indicator
  • grouping_variable: Stratification variable (optional)

docs.title: CORRELATIONS
docs.text:
Correlation between variables.

Triggers:

  • "correlation", "relationship", "association"

Variables Extracted:

  • primary_variable: First variable
  • grouping_variable: Second variable (if specified)
  • If no variables specified, compute correlation matrix

docs.title: Fuzzy Matching
docs.text:
Maps query terms to actual column names:

def _fuzzy_match_variable(query_term: str) -> Optional[str]:
    # Direct match
    if query_term in columns:
        return query_term

    # Fuzzy match with difflib
    matches = get_close_matches(
        query_term.lower(),
        [c.lower() for c in columns],
        n=1,
        cutoff=0.6
    )

    return matches[0] if matches else None

Examples:

  • "age" → age_years, patient_age
  • "died" → mortality, death
  • "treat" → treatment_arm, treatment

docs.title: Synonym Handling
docs.text:
Built-in synonym mapping:

SYNONYMS = {
    'age': ['age_years', 'patient_age', 'age_at_admission'],
    'mortality': ['died', 'death', 'deceased', 'expired'],
    'treatment': ['tx', 'therapy', 'intervention'],
    'outcome': ['result', 'endpoint', 'event']
}

docs.title: Query Templates
docs.text:
Pre-computed template library with embeddings:

templates = [
    {
        "template": "compare {outcome} by {group}",
        "intent": "COMPARE_GROUPS",
        "slots": ["outcome", "group"]
    },
    {
        "template": "what predicts {outcome}",
        "intent": "FIND_PREDICTORS",
        "slots": ["outcome"]
    },
    # ... more templates
]

Templates are built dynamically from semantic layer metadata.

docs.title: Confidence Thresholds
docs.text:
• >90%: High confidence (Tier 1 pattern match)
  • 75-90%: Good confidence (Tier 2 semantic match)
  • 50-75%: Medium confidence (show interpretation, ask for confirmation)
  • <50%: Low confidence (ask clarifying questions or use structured input)

docs.title: Unknown Variables
docs.text:
If extracted variable doesn't exist:

  1. Show "Variable not found: X"
  2. Suggest similar variables
  3. Allow user to select from dropdown

docs.title: Ambiguous Intent
docs.text:
If confidence <50%:

  1. Show possible interpretations
  2. Ask user to select
  3. Learn from user's choice (future enhancement)

docs.title: Invalid Combinations
docs.text:
If requested analysis doesn't match variable types:

  1. Explain incompatibility
  2. Suggest appropriate analysis
  3. Allow user to override

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: Metric Tier 1 Tier 2 Tier 3 Latency <1ms ~50ms ~2-5s Accuracy ~95% ~85% ~70% Coverage ~40% ~80% ~100% Privacy ✅ Local ✅ Local ⚠️ API

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
1. Learning from corrections: Update template weights based on user feedback
  2. Multi-step queries: "Compare survival by treatment, then stratify by age"
  3. Conditional filters: "Show mortality for ICU patients only"
  4. Time constraints: "30-day mortality" → extract timeframe
  5. Custom templates: Allow users to add domain-specific query patterns

docs.title: NL Query → Semantic Layer
docs.text:
# Phase 3: Enhanced QuestionEngine
class QuestionEngine:
    @staticmethod
    def parse_natural_language_query(
        query: str,
        semantic_layer: SemanticLayer
    ) -> AnalysisIntent:
        # 1. Get semantic layer metadata
        config = semantic_layer.config

        # 2. Extract available entities
        outcomes = list(config.get('outcomes', {}).keys())
        variables = list(config.get('column_mapping', {}).values())

        # 3. Use embeddings to match query to entities
        matched_outcome = match_entity(query, outcomes)
        matched_variables = match_entities(query, variables)

        # 4. Infer intent
        intent = infer_intent_from_query(query)

        return AnalysisIntent(
            intent=intent,
            outcome=matched_outcome,
            variables=matched_variables
        )

docs.title: Step 2: Implement Dataset Class
docs.text:
# src/clinical_analytics/datasets/my_dataset/definition.py
from clinical_analytics.core.dataset import ClinicalDataset
from clinical_analytics.core.semantic import SemanticLayer
from clinical_analytics.core.mapper import load_dataset_config

class MyDataset(ClinicalDataset):
    def __init__(self, source_path=None):
        self.config = load_dataset_config('my_new_dataset')
        if source_path is None:
            source_path = self.config['init_params']['source_path']
        super().__init__(name="my_new_dataset", source_path=source_path)
        self.semantic = SemanticLayer('my_new_dataset', config=self.config)

    def validate(self) -> bool:
        return self.source_path.exists() if self.source_path else False

    def load(self) -> None:
        if not self.validate():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Source not found: {self.source_path}")
        print(f"Semantic layer initialized for {self.name}")

    def get_cohort(self, **filters) -> pd.DataFrame:
        outcome_col = filters.get("target_outcome")
        filter_only = {k: v for k, v in filters.items() if k != "target_outcome"}
        return self.semantic.get_cohort(
            outcome_col=outcome_col,
            filters=filter_only
        )

docs.title: Step 3: Register in __init__.py
docs.text:
# src/clinical_analytics/datasets/__init__.py
from .my_dataset.definition import MyDataset

That's it! The registry auto-discovers it, UI shows it, query builder works.

docs.title: 🔍 Query Builder Usage
docs.text:
The query builder is fully config-driven:

  1. Metrics come from metrics section in config
  2. Dimensions come from dimensions section in config
  3. Filters come from filters section in config
  4. SQL is generated behind the scenes via Ibis

  sex,
  AVG(outcome_hospitalized) as "Hospitalization Rate",
  COUNT(*) as "Patient Count"
FROM covid_ms_raw
WHERE covid19_confirmed_case = 'confirmed'
GROUP BY age_group, sex

def compute_odds_ratio(a: int, b: int, c: int, d: int) -> float:

docs.title: Packaging the desktop app
docs.text: Step 1 of the installer work: the backend runs from an installed, read-only, relocated location with no network, and Electron owns its lifecycle. Steps 2-6 (bundled Python runtime, signing, .dmg/.msi) build on this.

docs.title: Supported platforms
docs.text:
Platform Minimum Why macOS 13 (Ventura), Apple silicon and Intel onnxruntime==1.23.2 ships macosx_13_0_arm64 and macosx_13_0_x86_64 wheels for cp311-cp313. 1.24+ dropped Intel and needs macOS 14; macOS 12 has no cp313 wheel. Windows 10/11 x64 (arm64 also has wheels) Linux x86_64 / aarch64, glibc 2.28 (manylinux_2_28)

onnxruntime is pinned exactly in pyproject.toml; move the pin only to a release at least two weeks old that still covers the platforms above.

docs.title: What the installed backend reads, and from where
docs.text:
• Read-only files ship inside the package, under src/clinical_analytics/resources/ (config/*.yaml, the synthetic demo cohort demo/sample_cohort.csv, and the embedding model under models/). They are found with importlib.resources through clinical_analytics.core.resources, whatever the cwd. Nothing is written there.
  • Everything written (uploads, DuckDB store, session DB, caches) goes to the per-user data home (clinical_analytics.core.data_home).

docs.title: Embedding model
docs.text:
• sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 at revision 1110a243fdf4706b3f48f1d95db1a4f5529b4d41, its official ONNX export, run with ONNX Runtime and HF tokenizers (core/embeddings.py). Apache-2.0; see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
  • Build step: make fetch-embedding-model downloads the pinned files once and checks each SHA-256 (scripts/fetch_embedding_model.py). Run it before uv build; the sdist and the wheel both include the model ([tool.hatch.build] artifacts; a plain uv build builds the wheel from the sdist, so it has to be in both).
  • At start, serve.py checks the model is present and its SHA-256 is the pinned one (cached by size and mtime in the data home), and otherwise exits with code 2 and one line. It is never downloaded at runtime. CLINICAL_ANALYTICS_EMBEDDING_MODEL_DIR points at a model elsewhere.

docs.title: The backend as an Electron sidecar
docs.text:
Electron main (electron/src/backendSidecar.js) starts, checks and stops the backend:

Setting Default Notes CLINICAL_ANALYTICS_PYTHON ../.venv/bin/python (Windows ..\.venv\Scripts\python.exe) Step 2 points it at the bundled runtime CLINICAL_ANALYTICS_API_PORT 8000 Used if free, otherwise an OS-assigned port on 127.0.0.1 CLINICAL_ANALYTICS_BACKEND_TIMEOUT_MS 60000 Whole startup wait; each request also times out after 3 s CLINICAL_ANALYTICS_EXTERNAL_BACKEND=1 off Dev flow: use an already-running API (make run-api, scripts/run_app.sh)
  • Spawned as python -I -u -m clinical_analytics.api.serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port P --exit-with-parent <electron pid> --stop-on-stdin-close, with this launch's API token, from <userData>/backend (a folder of the app's own, not the home directory). -I (isolated mode) keeps the working directory and user site-packages off Python's import path and ignores every PYTHON* variable, so a json.py or .pth file in the user's files is never imported by the backend; the venv still finds its packages. -u keeps the output unbuffered.
  • A bad CLINICAL_ANALYTICS_API_PORT or CLINICAL_ANALYTICS_BACKEND_TIMEOUT_MS stops startup with a message naming the variable.
  • A startup window shows while it boots; the main window opens once /health answers and the server proves it knows the token. Failures show an error window (on exit code 2, serve.py's one-line reason). A backend that dies later gets a Restart / Quit dialog.
  • The page's CSP header allows connect-src to exactly that backend's origin.
  • Stop on quit: POSIX SIGTERM to the process group, SIGKILL after 10 s; Windows closes the backend's stdin (graceful), then taskkill /T /F after 10 s. If Electron dies, the closed stdin and the parent watchdog shut the backend down gracefully; it hard-exits only if that has not finished after 120 s. The watchdog checks that Electron's PID is still running (on Linux also that it is the same process, by start time), not that it is the direct parent, so a launcher between Electron and the interpreter is fine. Both lifelines set uvicorn's should_exit once the server has started; neither raises a signal.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• make smoke-installed: runs the default uv build (sdist, then the wheel from it), checks the wheel contains the model, installs it in a fresh venv outside the repo, starts the API from an unrelated cwd with a temp HOME/XDG data home (in a loopback-only network namespace when available), uploads the synthetic cohort and runs a query. Also in CI.
  • cd electron && xvfb-run -a npx playwright test -c playwright.native.config.js: the app starts its own backend, the CSP blocks other loopback ports, a crashed backend can be restarted, and no backend is left after a quit or a SIGKILL of Electron.

docs.title: Known gap for the storage owner
docs.text: A graceful stop lets in-flight requests finish. If the process is killed hard mid-upload (power loss, or the 120 s fallback), UserDatasetStorage.save_upload can leave a partial raw CSV and its metadata JSON is rewritten in place under a lock rather than written to a temp file and renamed.

docs.title: Testing Philosophy
docs.text:
• Write tests first (TDD when possible)
  • Test behavior, not implementation
  • Keep tests fast (<1s per unit test)
  • Use fixtures for common test data
  • Mock external dependencies (APIs, file I/O)

docs.title: Test Structure
docs.text:
tests/
├── conftest.py           # Shared fixtures (check here first)
├── core/                 # Core module tests
├── api/                  # FastAPI tests
├── ui/                   # Streamlit-oriented tests
├── datasets/, analysis/, e2e/, ...
└── fixtures/             # Static files

Authoritative conventions: tests/AGENTS.md at the repository root (fixtures, Polars asserts, naming).

docs.title: Running tests (Makefile first)
docs.text:
Use make targets so markers, parallelism, and the project uv environment stay aligned with CI.

make install-dev
make test-fast           # Default pre-PR feedback (skips slow)
make test                # Full suite (parallel)
make test-core           # tests/core only
make test-ui             # tests/ui only
make test-api            # tests/api
make test-e2e            # Python e2e under tests/e2e
make test-electron-e2e   # Playwright in electron/ (after cd electron && npm ci)
make test-cov-check      # Coverage gate (67% minimum)

docs.title: Optional: PYTEST_ARGS
docs.text:
Append extra pytest flags (for example -k, -x, -vv). Recipe lines already pin the test directory or tests/ root, so use this for filters and verbosity, not as a substitute for choosing the right make test-* target.

make test-ui-serial PYTEST_ARGS='-k my_test_name -xvs'

For single-file debugging, red-phase uv run pytest path/to/test.py is acceptable per project rules; green phase should still go through make test-* where possible.

docs.title: Unit Test Example
docs.text:
import pytest
from clinical_analytics.core.nl_query_engine import NLQueryEngine, QueryIntent


def test_pattern_matching_compare_groups():
    """Test pattern matching for group comparison queries."""
    # Arrange
    engine = NLQueryEngine(semantic_layer=None)  # Mock semantic layer

    # Act
    intent = engine._pattern_match("compare mortality by treatment")

    # Assert
    assert intent is not None
    assert intent.intent_type == "COMPARE_GROUPS"
    assert intent.confidence > 0.9


def test_fuzzy_variable_matching():
    """Test fuzzy matching of variable names."""
    engine = NLQueryEngine(semantic_layer=None)
    engine.semantic_layer = MockSemanticLayer(columns=["age_years", "mortality", "treatment_arm"])

    result = engine._fuzzy_match_variable("age")

    assert result == "age_years"


def test_invalid_query_raises_error():
    """Test that invalid queries raise appropriate errors."""
    engine = NLQueryEngine(semantic_layer=None)

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Query cannot be empty"):
        engine.parse_query("")

@pytest.mark.parametrize("query,expected_intent", [
    ("compare mortality by treatment", "COMPARE_GROUPS"),
    ("what predicts mortality", "FIND_PREDICTORS"),
    ("survival analysis", "SURVIVAL"),
    ("correlation between age and outcome", "CORRELATIONS"),
    ("descriptive statistics", "DESCRIBE"),
])

docs.title: Testing Statistical Functions
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from scipy import stats


def test_t_test():
    """Test t-test implementation."""
    group_a = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
    group_b = np.array([3, 4, 5, 6, 7])

    result = run_t_test(group_a, group_b)

    # Verify with scipy
    expected = stats.ttest_ind(group_a, group_b)

    assert np.isclose(result['t_statistic'], expected.statistic)
    assert np.isclose(result['p_value'], expected.pvalue)


def test_logistic_regression():
    """Test logistic regression."""
    X = np.random.randn(100, 2)
    y = np.random.binomial(1, 0.5, 100)

    result = run_logistic_regression(X, y)

    assert 'coefficients' in result
    assert 'p_values' in result
    assert 'auc' in result
    assert 0 <= result['auc'] <= 1

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Arrange-Act-Assert: Structure tests clearly
  2. One assertion per test: Tests should be focused
  3. Descriptive names: test_pattern_matching_compare_groups not test1
  4. Use fixtures: Share setup code
  5. Mock external dependencies: Keep tests fast and reliable
  6. Test edge cases: Empty input, missing data, invalid types
  7. Test error handling: Verify exceptions are raised correctly
