  • Strategy Pattern: https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/strategy
  • Protocol (PEP 544): https://peps.python.org/pep-0544/

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Proposed (2026-11-13). Base: origin/main @ 9ef3fe1. Reference design; the steel thread in Purpose and steel thread decides which part is built next.

Revised 2026-11-14 (base origin/main @ 16e94c6), after an outside review and the COVID-MS baseline from #104:

  • Step 3 takes the alias step (§1.4) and the column-choice hold (§5.1) from later PRs, and confirmations re-run the stored plan (§6.3).
  • Step 4 is cut down to what #106 built (§2.1). The CTE and __pid lineage machinery (§4.1–4.2) waits until after MVP, and only if the corpus needs it. A per-answer check of every combination of filters, per group, and a step-by-step patient count are added on both paths (§4.5).
  • Differencing across questions moves from a session ledger to a dataset-version log, at step 6 (§4.4, §12).
  • The harness grades answered right and correctly held separately, and adds a held-out question set (§11.3).
  • These wait: revisions (§1.3), ODPS (§1.5), review UI (§1.6), charts (§9), lineage (§10) and packaging.

docs.title: 0. What exists today (constraints this design keeps)
docs.text:
• The intent path. NLQueryEngine (core/nl_query_engine.py) runs pattern, then embedding, then LLM tiers. It produces QueryPlan (core/query_plan.py:103, five intents). QueryService.ask (core/query_service.py) does the locked prepare, an unlocked parse, then a locked _finish. _finish runs validation, measurement and grouping refusals, answer_checks findings, word accounting, execute_query_plan, then format_execution_result, present_analysis.
  • Privacy. The privacy core is core/result_presentation.py:
  • _suppress_lines(cells, lines, floors) does primary and secondary suppression for any set of lines with known totals.
  • suppress_with_exclusions treats n_filtered_out as a hidden cell.
  • Small groups are folded into OTHER_LABEL.
  • MIN_CELL_SIZE = SMALL_CELL_THRESHOLD = 11 (contracts/config.py, nl_query.yaml).
  • Statistics. analysis/compute.py::compute_analysis_by_type(df, context, entity_key) takes a Polars frame and an AnalysisContext. It runs t-test, ANOVA, chi-square, Fisher, logistic regression with ORs and CIs, Kaplan–Meier, log-rank, Cox and correlation. Analysis floors are in analysis/sample_floors.py.
  • Contract. contracts/builder.py::build_contract writes one ODCS v3.2.0 file per upload version to contracts/<upload_id>/<version>.odcs.yaml, write-once (store.write_contract).
  • It covers only the unified object.
  • It already carries description, synonyms, unit, clinicalSemanticType, enum codebook and the phi tag from ResolvedDatasetMetadata.
  • Only the DQ checks read it.
  • contracts/config.py says "Not bumped yet when a patch is accepted later: the re-contract trigger is deferred."
  • Declarations. contracts/declarations.py stores grain and LevelMapping per version in declarations.json.
  • AutoContext. core/autocontext.py is built separately, from the alias index and get_column_metadata. It is called only from NLQueryEngine._llm_parse (around line 2311).
  • It ships min, max and top_values with counts, and does not filter small cells. That is a privacy gap.
  • It crashed on uploads.
  • Metadata patches (ADR011). core/metadata_patch.py, core/overlay_store.py and api/routes/enrichments.py provide pending, accept, reject, revert and history. Patch provenance can be llm, user or dictionary.
  • Documentation (ADR004). core/doc_parser.py::extract_context_from_docs feeds SchemaInference.parse_dictionary_text, which returns DictionaryMetadata (descriptions, types, valid values, codebooks).
  • Storage.
  • Each stored table is parquet/{upload_id}_{table}_{version}.parquet (table_parquet_path).
  • The cohort is parquet/{upload_id}__cohort_{...}.parquet.
  • Metadata holds tables, parquet_paths and relationships.
  • Dependencies. sqlglot 30.31.0 is already in uv.lock, pulled in by Ibis 12. DuckDB is 2.0.x.
  • Model. nl_query.yaml sets the default to llama3.1:8b with fallback llama3.2:3b. This spec plans for 3B: it is the smallest model the app falls back to (ollama_fallback_model), so the design has to work at that size. OllamaClient.generate posts to /api/generate, JSON mode, with no tool calling.

docs.title: 1. The contract as the single context
1.1 Shape
docs.text:
There is one ODCS v3.2.0 document per (upload_id, dataset_version, revision). There is one schema[] object per stored table plus unified (the cohort). Top-level customProperties hold uploadId, datasetVersion, revision, minCellSize, metadataPatchIds, declarations and productRef.

Per table object:

- name: labevents
  physicalName: labevents            # view name the SQL path exposes
  logicalType: object
  description: "Laboratory measurements ..."          # doc / patch / user
  dataGranularityDescription: "One row per lab result"
  customProperties:
    - {property: grain, value: event}                 # patient | visit | event | reference
    - {property: patientKey, value: subject_id}       # null for reference tables
    - {property: timeColumn, value: charttime}
    - {property: privacyClass, value: patient_level}  # patient_level | public_aggregate
  relationships:                                      # ODCS v3.1+ relationships
    - {type: foreignKey, from: labevents.subject_id, to: patients.subject_id, customProperties: [{property: cardinality, value: many_to_one}]}
    - {type: foreignKey, from: labevents.hadm_id, to: admissions.hadm_id, customProperties: [{property: cardinality, value: many_to_one}]}
  properties:
    - name: valuenum
      physicalName: valuenum
      logicalType: number
      physicalType: Float64
      businessName: "Lab value"
      description: "..."
      synonyms: [{synonym: result}]
      classification: public|restricted
      tags: [phi]                                      # only when PHI
      enum: [{value: 1, label: "Positive"}]            # documented codebook, never observed values
      customProperties:
        - {property: semanticType, value: measurement} # identifier|demographic|clinical|temporal|outcome|measurement|coded|rate|count|free_text
        - {property: unit, value: "mg/dL"}
        - {property: unitSource, value: dictionary}    # dictionary|patch|user|header|assumed
        - {property: missingTokens, value: ["NA", "-999"]}
        - {property: privacyClass, value: none}        # identifier | phi | public_aggregate | none
        - {property: concept, value: {system: LOINC, code: "2160-0", display: "Creatinine [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma"}}
        - {property: weightColumn, value: population}  # for rate columns: required to pool
        - {property: provenance, value: {description: "dictionary:mimic_iv_demo_dictionary.pdf#p4", unit: "patch:p_123"}}

The rule from builder.py stays: observed values (levels, min and max) are never written into the contract. Samples are computed when the prompt is rendered (see 1.4).

docs.title: 1.2 Sources, in precedence order (last wins)
docs.text:
1. Inference. dtype; classify_variable; header codebooks (code_labels); parse_column_name units; MultiTableHandler.classify_tables grain and keys; metadata["relationships"].
  2. Documentation. doc_parser.extract_context_from_docs feeds SchemaInference.parse_dictionary_text, which returns DictionaryMetadata. Each entry becomes a MetadataPatch(provenance="dictionary"):
  3. When the dictionary names the column exactly (normalised), the patch is auto-accepted.
  4. When the match is fuzzy, the patch stays PENDING.
  5. Either way, documentation flows through the one ADR011 review flow.
  6. Accepted ADR011 patches, from llm, user or dictionary.
  7. Declarations. Grain, level merges and units (a new UnitDeclaration) from declarations.json, copied into customProperties.declarations.
  8. Vocabulary (P4). contracts/vocabulary.py matches columns to a curated LOINC subset by name, synonym and unit. Matches are proposed as pending SET_CONCEPT patches (a new PatchOperation). Accepted concepts add synonyms to the alias index.

docs.title: 1.3 Revisions
docs.text:
• Files. Revision 0 stays at the existing write-once path. Later revisions go to contracts/<upload_id>/<dataset_version>/rev-<NNNN>.odcs.yaml and version: 1.<N>.0. The pointer .../current.json ({"revision": N, "sha256": ...}) is written last through storage/atomic.py as the commit point.
  • New module contracts/revisions.py:
  • ContractChange is a union: PatchDecision | DeclarationStored | UserEdit | PortChange.
  • apply_change(contract: OpenDataContractStandard, change: ContractChange) -> OpenDataContractStandard is a pure transform, and is unit-tested.
  • revise(data_dir, upload_id, dataset_version, change) -> ContractRef runs under storage/metadata_lock.
  • current_contract(data_dir, upload_id, dataset_version) -> tuple[DatasetContract, ContractRef].
  • ContractRef is a frozen dataclass (upload_id, dataset_version, revision, sha256), shown as "{upload_id}/{version}@1.{rev}.0#{sha12}".
  • Triggers. A new revision comes from:
  • patch accept, reject or revert (OverlayStore.accept_patch and the others call revise);
  • QueryService._declare;
  • a user edit in the review UI;
  • a product-port change.

This retires the "re-contract trigger is deferred" note. - Typed read view. contracts/context.py::DatasetContract is a typed facade over the ODCS model: tables: dict[str, TableSpec] and TableSpec.columns: dict[str, ColumnSpec]. The gate and the renderer read only this.

docs.title: 1.4 Context rendering (replaces AutoContext's inputs)
docs.text:
contracts/context.py:

def render_context(contract: DatasetContract, ref: ContractRef, *, purpose: Literal["intent", "sql"],
                   question: str, budget_tokens: int, sampler: SafeSampler | None,
                   tables: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> RenderedContext
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RenderedContext: text: str; tables: tuple[str, ...]; columns: tuple[str, ...]; tokens: int; ref: ContractRef
  • Relevance. Columns are scored with the existing MiniLM core/embeddings.py over businessName, description, synonyms and concept display. The renderer always includes:
  • every key and timeColumn of each chosen table;
  • each relationship between chosen tables.
  • Line format, one per column: labevents.valuenum NUMBER unit=mg/dL type=measurement concept=LOINC:2160-0 "Creatinine" — Lab value. levels: …
  • Budget. Counted with tiktoken, as today. Drop order when over budget:
  • samples;
  • codebook entries beyond 12;
  • descriptions truncated to 160 characters;
  • least-relevant non-key columns.
  • SafeSampler (contracts/sampling.py) reads the sandbox connection (section 3):
  • Categorical, coded or demographic columns with privacyClass none. Levels come from SELECT col FROM v GROUP BY col HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT key) >= MIN_CELL_SIZE ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT key) DESC LIMIT 12. No counts are sent to the model. Rows are used when the table has no key, and a reference table gets no samples. A column with more than MAX_GROUP_LEVELS levels gets "many values" and no samples.
  • Numeric columns. p05, p50 and p95 to 2 significant figures, only when at least 5 * MIN_CELL_SIZE patients have a value. Never min or max.
  • Dates. Year of p05 and p95 only.
  • Identifier, PHI and free-text columns. No samples, ever.
  • Intent path. build_autocontext(...) keeps its signature as a thin adapter: it calls render_context(purpose="intent") and maps the result to the existing AutoContext and ColumnContext. Its stats drop min, max and counted top_values. _llm_parse passes the ContractRef. This removes the crashing reconstruction path (_reconstruct_inferred_schema_from_semantic_layer).
  • Aliases (step 3; was P4). SemanticLayer._build_alias_index adds contract synonyms, descriptions and codebook labels, and word accounting reads them. A question word counts as used when the contract accounts for it: "MS type" matches ms_type2's description, and "admitted" matches covid19_admission_hospital's. The model and the planner then read only the contract. This is the general form of the word-by-word rules on fix/covid-ms-holds. Concept displays follow with the P4 vocabulary.

docs.title: 1.5 ODPS product file (P5)
docs.text:
contracts/<upload_id>/<dataset_version>/product.odps.yaml follows the Bitol Open Data Product Standard: - outputPorts lists the views the SQL path may query (name, contractRef). - customProperties holds minCellSize, sqlProfile: "mdde-sql-1" (allowlist version), maxCoreRows: 5000, timeoutSeconds: 10, maxJoins (per model tier).

The user can hide a table, such as free-text notes, from questions. Hiding a table removes its port and makes a new revision. Module: contracts/product.py::current_product(...) -> DataProduct.

docs.title: 1.6 Review in the app
docs.text:
• API. Extend api/routes/enrichments.py:
  • GET /datasets/{id}/contract returns the rendered tables and columns, the provenance of each field, and ContractRef.
  • GET /datasets/{id}/contract/revisions returns [{revision, ts, change_summary}].
  • PATCH /datasets/{id}/contract/columns/{table}/{column} is a user edit. It becomes a MetadataPatch(provenance="user") that is accepted on creation.
  • Existing pending, accept, reject and revert are unchanged; each now returns the new ContractRef.
  • Electron. Turn electron/src/enrichmentPanel.js into a contract panel: a table, then columns, each with description, unit, type, codebook and privacy. Pending suggestions show inline with Accept and Reject. patchHistoryPanel.js shows revisions.

docs.title: 2. Static validation (src/clinical_analytics/sql/validate.py)
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ValidatedQuery:
    canonical_sql: str               # sqlglot-generated from the checked AST (what runs)
    ast: sqlglot.exp.Expression
    core: CoreSplit                  # section 4.2
    column_use: ColumnUse            # section 5.1
    views: frozenset[str]
def validate_sql(sql: str, catalog: SqlCatalog, product: DataProduct) -> ValidatedQuery  # raises SqlRefusal(reason: str)

Steps, each with a plain-language SqlRefusal:

  1. One statement. duckdb.extract_statements(sql) must return exactly 1 statement of StatementType.SELECT. DuckDB's own parser is the authority for statement type.
  2. Parse. sqlglot.parse_one(sql, dialect="duckdb"). The root must be Select, or Select with With, or Union (constrained in step 8).
  3. Forbidden node types anywhere: Create, Insert, Update, Delete, Drop, Alter, Copy, Attach, Pragma, Set, Command, Into, recursive With, Lateral, and Table function calls.
  4. Qualify. sqlglot.optimizer.qualify.qualify(ast, schema=catalog.sqlglot_schema(), dialect="duckdb", expand_stars=True, validate_qualify_columns=True). Every column resolves to a view.column in the contract, which is the gate's "every column must exist" rule. Unknown tables or tables not in product.outputPorts are refused.
  5. Function allowlist. sql/functions.py::ALLOWED: dict[str, FunctionRule]. Anything not listed is refused, including all table functions, read_*, glob, query, getenv, current_setting, duckdb_*, pragma_*, random, uuid, now and current_date, which break reproducibility.
  6. Aggregates: count, count(distinct), count_if, sum, avg, median, quantile_cont, min, max, stddev_samp, var_samp, bool_and, bool_or.
  7. Scalars: arithmetic, round, floor, ceil, abs, ln, exp, sqrt, power, greatest, least, coalesce, nullif, CASE, cast/try_cast, lower, upper, trim, length, substring, contains, starts_with, regexp_matches with a literal pattern of 100 characters or fewer, date_trunc, date_part/extract, year, month, date_diff, date_add with interval literals, make_date, strftime.
  8. Windows: row_number, rank, dense_rank, lag, lead, first_value, last_value, and sum, count or avg OVER.
  9. Bounded series: range and generate_series with literal bounds and at most 1000 values, for calendar spines.
  10. Refused with a pointer: corr, regr_*, covar_*, mode, list, array_agg, string_agg, histogram, arg_min, arg_max, any_value and first in aggregates.
  11. Privacy-class rules:
  12. Identifier columns may appear only in join conditions, COUNT(DISTINCT key), PARTITION BY and GROUP BY of non-final blocks. They may never be projected in the final output, grouped at the final block, or compared with a literal. A comparison with a literal would be a question about one patient.
  13. PHI columns may appear only inside year(), date_trunc('year'|'month', …), date_diff or predicates. They may never be projected raw.
  14. Limits.
  15. At most product.maxJoins joins: 1 for 3B, 4 for 7–8B.
  16. AST size of 400 nodes or fewer.
  17. CTE depth of 6 or less.
  18. An existing LIMIT above 5000 is refused.
  19. Contract gate (P5), in contracts/gate.py, section 5.
  20. Shape. The core/post split of section 4.2 must succeed, or the query is refused with the reason for that pattern.

canonical_sql = ast.sql(dialect="duckdb") after the privacy rewrite. What runs is always text generated from the AST that was checked, never the model's text.

docs.title: 2.1 Step 4 scope: what #106 built
docs.text:
Step 4 builds this smaller version, not all of §2–§4. The rest waits until the corpus needs it.

  • One table, the contract's unified object. No joins, CTEs, subqueries, UNION, ROLLUP, CUBE or GROUPING SETS.
  • At most one dimension. It may be any row-level expression, such as CASE bands, year() or date_trunc.
  • Measures are arithmetic over count(*), count(col), count(DISTINCT id), count_if, sum, avg, median, quantile_cont and stddev/var_samp, each with an optional FILTER. Value aggregates take a bare numeric column.
  • Refused: listings, HAVING, QUALIFY, windows, MIN/MAX, more than 200 groups, and visit-level data (an ID that repeats).
  • Not needed yet: the core/post split and __pid lineage (§4.1–4.2), because there are no per-patient CTEs.
  • sqlglot is declared directly in pyproject.toml with a major-version bound. The validator's safety depends on its AST, so an Ibis upgrade must not change it silently.

docs.title: 3. Sandboxed execution (sql/sandbox.py)
docs.text:
class SandboxConnection:
    def __init__(self, catalog: SqlCatalog, *, memory_limit: DuckdbMemoryLimit, threads: int): ...
    def run(self, sql: str, *, timeout_s: float, max_rows: int) -> pl.DataFrame  # raises SqlTimeout, SqlTooManyRows
  • Separate connection. A separate in-memory duckdb.connect(":memory:", config={...}) per leased dataset version, owned by the SemanticLayer lease (api/layer_cache.py). It is never the Ibis connection, so the model's SQL can't touch layer state.
  • Connect config:
  • enable_external_access=false;
  • allowed_paths=[<exact parquet files from metadata["parquet_paths"] and the cohort>];
  • autoinstall_known_extensions=false, autoload_known_extensions=false, allow_community_extensions=false, allow_unsigned_extensions=false;
  • memory_limit set to the layer's share (CACHED_LAYER_MEMORY_LIMIT), threads=DUCKDB_THREADS;
  • max_temp_directory_size='0B'.
  • Catalog views. SqlCatalog.from_contract(contract, metadata) creates views like CREATE VIEW "labevents" AS SELECT <typed columns, missing tokens to NULL, confirmed LevelMapping merges as CASE> FROM read_parquet(?). This gives the SQL path the same merged levels as the intent path's remap_levels. Then SET lock_configuration=true.
  • Read-only. Only views exist, the validator admits only SELECT, and external access is off. Even a validator bypass can't read or write files or attach a database. PR4 has a test that runs read_text('/etc/passwd'), COPY and ATTACH directly on the connection and expects errors.
  • Time limit. A threading.Timer(timeout_s, con.interrupt).
  • Row limit. The core is wrapped as SELECT * FROM (<core>) LIMIT max_rows+1. Getting more than max_rows rows is refused ("too many groups to check for small cells").
  • Locking. Its own lock. It is not the layer's _con_lock, so the SQL path never blocks intent questions.

docs.title: 4.1 Lineage of the patient key
docs.text:
Waits until after MVP, and only if the corpus needs it (§2.1). The step 4 path has no CTEs.

Every block (CTE, subquery or final) is classified by classify_block(select, catalog) -> BlockKind:

  • row_level: no GROUP BY or aggregate. The rewriter adds <view>.<patientKey> AS __pid to the projection when missing. It is taken from the leftmost patient-bearing source, and a join on declared keys keeps it.
  • per_patient: GROUP BY includes __pid or the patient key. __pid is kept as a group key, and windows PARTITION BY __pid are allowed.
  • core: the one aggregating block whose GROUP BY does not include the patient key. It must read only row_level or per_patient inputs, or reference tables.
  • post: blocks above the core that read only the core's output.

Refused: - an aggregation not by patient that feeds another aggregation, which loses lineage and is how averaged rates get pooled; - two core blocks; - a patient-bearing input whose __pid can't be derived.

docs.title: 4.2 Core/post split and companions
docs.text:
CoreSplit(core_sql, post_sql | None, dims: list[str], measures: list[MeasureSpec]).

  • Core rewrite. For the core block with dimensions D:
  • Add COUNT(DISTINCT __pid) AS __n.
  • For every aggregate node agg(arg) [FILTER (WHERE f)] inside output expression m_i, add:
    • COUNT(DISTINCT __pid) FILTER (WHERE f AND arg IS NOT NULL) AS __nn_i_k, the patients with a value;
    • for indicator arguments only, COUNT(DISTINCT __pid) FILTER (WHERE f AND arg IS NOT NULL AND arg <> 0 AND arg IS NOT FALSE) AS __nz_i_k.
  • An argument is an indicator when, statically, it is a boolean, a comparison, or a CASE with constant 0/1 or NULL branches. At runtime, a numeric argument with 2 or fewer distinct values in the core input is also treated as one.
  • COUNT(*), COUNT(x), SUM(indicator), AVG(indicator) and count_if are additive patient-derived measures.
  • Windows inside the core. SUM|COUNT|AVG(agg) OVER (PARTITION BY subset of D), used for shares of a total, stay in the core and inherit the companions of their row.
  • Moved to post. HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT, QUALIFY, LAG, LEAD and the rank family are lifted out of the core into post. Applied before suppression, a HAVING n > 10 would turn the removed groups into one cell that can be worked out from the total.
  • Reference counts, computed by the runtime in the same sandbox call:
  • P_all: distinct patients in the dataset, from cached base counts;
  • P_core: distinct __pid in the core's input after WHERE;
  • P_cte[j]: for each patient-bearing CTE j whose pids are a superset of the core input, checked with NOT EXISTS. This is the "C. diff positives" cohort a user could count separately.

docs.title: 4.3 Suppression (reuses _suppress_lines)
docs.text:
Step 4 design (#106). #106 goes further than the text below in three places, and those are the design:

  1. WHERE becomes FILTER. The patients the whole WHERE removes are counted per group and per aggregate partition, not only against the whole table. So the same query run without its WHERE can't difference out a small group. The terms of the WHERE are not checked against each other, and two filtered aggregates are not checked against each other; §4.5 adds that.
  2. Value aggregates take bare columns only. avg(1000*(x>5) + x/1e6) would encode a count that the indicator rule misses.
  3. No error can depend on the data. Row expressions run inside TRY(...) and measures in DOUBLE, so CASE WHEN <one patient> THEN CAST('x' AS INT) and integer overflow can't act as an oracle.

The rest of this section describes the full design for when the core/post split exists.

suppress_core(frame, split, refs) -> SuppressedCore(rows, hidden: set[CellKey], folded: bool, notes).

  • Cells.
  • __n per row.
  • For additive measures: nz, zeros = nn − nz and nulls = __n − nn per row.
  • Virtual cells, never shown: outside_all = P_all − P_core and outside_j = P_cte[j] − P_core. They work the way suppress_with_exclusions treats n_filtered_out.
  • Lines (sets whose total is treated as known):
  • (a) For each count family, all rows plus outside_all, which totals P_all. The same again with outside_j for each reference CTE.
  • (b) Within a row, {nz, zeros, nulls}, which totals __n.
  • (c) For two or more dimensions, marginal lines per dimension, as suppress_count_matrix builds them.
  • (d) When rows overlap (section 6.2), the overlap Σ__n − P_core as a virtual cell in line (a).
  • Primary hiding. A cell is hidden when it is 1–10. Floors: MIN_GROUP_N for groups when a tool runs.
  • What a hidden cell does to its row.
  • Hidden __n: the whole row is folded into one OTHER_LABEL row whose measures are recomputed by re-running the core with those dimension values merged into one level. If that row is itself 1–10, it is dropped and the note says "groups of fewer than 11 patients are not shown". The labels of small groups are never shown, as in _fold_rows.
  • Hidden nz, zeros or nulls: every measure built on that aggregate shows SECONDARY_SUPPRESSED.
  • A continuous measure (mean, median, quantile) is shown only if nn ≥ MIN_CELL_SIZE.
  • MIN or MAX of a numeric is shown under the same rule. MIN or MAX of a date or timestamp is refused statically unless it is wrapped in year() or date_trunc.
  • Post stage. The post SQL runs in the sandbox over the suppressed, folded core registered as core (Arrow), with hidden cells as NULL and the __* columns dropped. LAG over a hidden cell gives NULL, and ranks run over shown rows only, so the post stage can't leak. The note says "ranked among groups of at least 11 patients".

docs.title: 4.4 Patterns that can't be enforced (refused, with the text shown)
docs.text: Pattern Why Refusal Final output not aggregated (patient listings, SELECT *) Each row is one patient "This would list individual patients." Aggregation of aggregates not grouped by patient Lineage to patients is lost "Averaging group results hides how many patients each one has. Ask for the measure over patients directly." UNION, INTERSECT or EXCEPT at or above the core; GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP, CUBE Row overlap can't be bounded statically (a "Both" row) "Combined or total rows can reveal small groups." Row-level UNION ALL of event tables that each carry __pid is allowed. Scalar or correlated subqueries in the final SELECT Hidden extra cohorts "Write it as a WITH step." list, string_agg, array_agg, arg_min/max, any_value, mode on text Return a patient's value Function refused Identifier compared with a literal, or projected Single patient "A question about one patient." More than 5000 core groups, or the final group by is the patient key Every cell is small "Too many groups to check." Differences across separate questions (count(A) then count(A and p)) Caught when one answer's conditions include all of the other's and the groupings match, or the one with fewer conditions is not grouped (§4.5). Not caught otherwise: a changed threshold ("over 65", then "over 66") or a different grouping. Residual risk, stated in Purpose; docs/security/THREAT_MODEL.md gets the entry with #106. At step 6, a dataset-version log of shown counts refuses a count one filter change away from a count already shown (§12). It is kept per dataset version, not per session, because a new chat would reset a session ledger.

docs.title: 4.5 Per-answer filter check and step-by-step count (step 4, both paths)
docs.text:
This borrows two mechanisms. DataSHIELD's subset rule (R/dataFrameSubsetDS1.R) flags a subset that differs from its parent by a few rows; here it is strict and refuses. OHDSI ATLAS reports inclusion-rule attrition from a bitmask of which rules each person meets (Book of OHDSI, ch. 10).

What #106 checks today. Per group, #106 counts the patients its whole WHERE removes, and splits each aggregate's group into the rows it reads (FILTER, count_if, non-null values, each value of a coded column) and the rest. That stops a difference with the same query without its WHERE, and between a filtered and an unfiltered count. It does not compare two filtered aggregates, or the terms of one WHERE, with each other. On #106's branch (eb2eec5), SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE a = 1) - count(*) FILTER (WHERE a = 1 AND b = 1 AND c = 1) returns 5 on a synthetic table where 5 patients with a = 1 fail both b and c. The check below closes that. It goes into sql/privacy.py before ENABLE_SQL_QUERIES can be on by default, and into the question path with PR 6.

  • Conditions. An answer's conditions are every top-level AND term of its WHERE, of each FILTER and of each count_if, plus <column> IS NOT NULL for each column that a count(column) or a value aggregate reads. On the question path they are the plan's filters. Conditions are compared as rendered from the checked tree, so age > 65 and 65 < age are two conditions: stricter, never weaker.
  • Cells. Each condition becomes an indicator, coalesce(TRY(<condition>), false). NOT p is its own indicator, never computed as the opposite of p, because a row where p is NULL is false in both. One grouped query counts patients per group and per combination of indicators: 2^k cells per group, ATLAS's bitmask. For a value aggregate over a coded column (at most 20 values), each cell is split per value, as #106 already does.
  • The rule. Every cell is a count for _suppress_lines, with #106's lines: a group's cells add up to the group, and each cell across groups adds up to the same query without GROUP BY. A group's measures are shown only when none of its cells is hidden. An ungrouped answer with a hidden cell is withheld: "This answer, with its filters, would let a reader work out a count of 1 to 10 patients. Ask with fewer filters or a coarser grouping." Every count a shown answer reveals about its conditions is then a sum of cells that are each 0 or at least 11. This holds however the conditions are split, because every measure counts the rows that meet a set of them; splitting only decides how strict the check is. That covers:
  • dropping any set of filters, not only one. count(A) minus count(A and B and C) is the patients with A who fail B, C or both: three cells, each checked;
  • differencing inside one answer, through FILTER clauses, count_if or arithmetic between differently filtered counts;
  • a filter that removes 11 or more overall but 1–10 in one group, because cells are per group.
  • Fail closed. More than 4 conditions, IS NOT NULL terms included (16 cells per group, 3,200 at 200 groups), are refused, never checked in part. If the counting query fails, nothing is shown. Both paths read the threshold from SMALL_CELL_THRESHOLD and pass their cells to one shared function; only the counting query differs (DuckDB on the SQL path, Polars on the question path).
  • Across answers, without memory. The check never reads earlier answers, and it doesn't need to when one answer's conditions include all of the other's, and both group the same way or the one with fewer conditions is not grouped. Each count the answer with fewer conditions shows is then a sum of the other answer's cells, and that answer checked them all, whichever came first. That is why "count A, then count A and B" is safe. It is not because a later answer removes more patients: how many "A and B and C" removes from "A and B" is unrelated to how many "A and B" removed from "A". Answers whose conditions aren't nested, or that group differently, are the residual risk in §4.4.
  • The step-by-step count. Every answer shows the attrition line, CONSORT style: "1,141 patients → 612 women → 341 with RRMS", one step per condition in the order written. It is the cheapest form of "method shown". Each count in it is a sum of the answer's cells, so the counts are what get hidden, never only the steps: with 612 and 605 shown, a hidden step of 7 is still 7. A count is hidden when any cell it adds up is hidden. The shown counts, with the dataset total the app shows, are lines in the same _suppress_lines call, so complementary suppression hides more cells, and so more counts, until no hidden cell is the difference of two shown counts. In an answer with no hidden cell, every count and every step is already 0 or at least 11.
  • Tests. Each case above is an adversarial test, on synthetic data, on both paths: two filters dropped at once (the 5 patients who fail both B and C), nested FILTER differencing (the query above), a filter that removes 3 patients in one group and 40 overall, the attrition line 1,141 → 612 → 605 → 341, and a NULL-valued condition with its NOT. They join tests/sql/test_privacy_adversarial.py on #106 and the intent-path privacy tests.
  • Before the flag defaults on, add ACRO's dominance and p-ratio checks for sum and avg of continuous columns (#106 lists means as a residual risk).

docs.title: 5. Correctness guards and the P5 planner gate (contracts/gate.py)
docs.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GateResult: refusal: str | None; holds: list[str]; notes: list[str]
def check_sql(q: ValidatedQuery, contract: DatasetContract) -> GateResult
def check_plan(plan: QueryPlan, contract: DatasetContract) -> GateResult   # intent path too, called in QueryService._finish before execute

docs.title: 5.1 Using answer_checks on SQL
docs.text:
Add ColumnUse to core/answer_checks.py. Today the checks read a QueryPlan; this extracts the column-level inputs they need:

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ColumnUse:
    view: str
    statistic_columns: tuple[str, ...]   # args of avg/median/sum/stddev/quantile (non-indicator)
    group_columns: tuple[str, ...]       # core GROUP BY dims
    equality_values: tuple[tuple[str, Any], ...]  # col = 'literal', col IN (...)
    limit_columns: tuple[str, ...]       # any predicate column
    counted: Literal["patients", "rows"] | None
    statistic_kind: Literal["describe", "compare"] | None
def column_use_of_plan(plan: QueryPlan) -> ColumnUse            # adapter; existing behaviour
def data_findings(stats: ViewStats, use: ColumnUse, declarations, version, report) -> Findings

ViewStats is a protocol with rows(), distinct(col), missing(col), value_counts(col) and dtype(col). SemanticLayer implements it for the base view, and SandboxConnection implements it per view, with a cache per contract revision. The body of QueryService._data_findings moves into data_findings. Mapping:

Existing check SQL application grain_of, declared_visits, grain_hold_reason, missing_key_note Per patient-bearing view in the core input. A hold applies when the view's grain is undeclared and repeated and a count is COUNT(*) or COUNT(x) (rows). Tables the contract grains as event don't hold, but their counts are labelled "rows (events)". metric_refusal, statistic_refusal Every statistic_columns entry, so values like "<5" stored as text are refused. variant_findings Group columns and string equality literals. This gives the same hold and LevelMapping, and confirming it changes the catalog view and the contract revision. implausible_sentences Statistic and limit columns. grouped_count_refusal, share_refusal, varies_within_patient Core dims and indicator measures at visit grain. measurement_grouping_reason, grouping_problem Core dims, unless the dim is wrapped in a binning expression (floor(x/10)*10, CASE ranges, date_trunc). missingness_notes, report_notes All columns read. Word accounting (unjustified_elements) Replaced by sql/accounting.py::unasked_literals(question, history, ast). A WHERE literal or threshold that doesn't appear in the question, the earlier turns or a confirmed synonym is held: "The query limits to <x>, which the question did not mention."

Word-accounting holds on the question path (step 3). This borrows Data Formulator's mix of picking and typing.

  • Choose, don't rephrase. When the contract doesn't account for a word, the hold no longer says "rephrase it with a column or value" (core/word_accounting.py). It offers the 2–3 contract columns that best match the word, ranked by the existing MiniLM embeddings (§1.4), plus "none of these".
  • Saved once per dataset. The choice becomes an accepted MetadataPatch(provenance="user") synonym, so the contract accounts for the word from then on.
  • In the harness, a question with confirm: true picks the oracle's column. Its grade is reported as right after one clarification, apart from both answered right and correctly held (§11.3).
  • At step 4, a word-accounting hold routes to model-written SQL instead (§6.4). unasked_literals still holds a WHERE literal the question never asked for.

Cap on hand-written vocabulary rules. No question-specific vocabulary goes into word_accounting.py or question_vocabulary.py; new words come from the contract. From fix/covid-ms-holds, only dataset-independent grammar merges: "broken down by" read as "by", and joining a hyphenated name when a column spells it that way. Domain verbs such as PLACE_VERBS do not. The count of hand-written rules after that merge is the cap: a new rule must replace one. Without the cap, rules get tuned to the 15 questions that score them.

docs.title: 5.2 Gate rules
docs.text:
• Columns exist. Done by qualify against the contract schema.
  • Joins use declared keys. Every JOIN ON must be a conjunction of equalities that match a contract relationships entry, in either direction. Extra conjuncts may only be inequalities or BETWEEN on temporal columns (time windows), or literal filters. Cross joins are refused, except to a reference table or a range spine.
  • Fan-out. After a one_to_many join, SUM, AVG or COUNT(*) of a column from the "one" side is refused ("counted once per ").
  • Means of codes. AVG, SUM, MEDIAN or STDDEV of semanticType ∈ {coded, identifier, demographic-categorical}, or of a column with enum, is refused with the same wording as numeric_text.statistic_refusal. A binary 0/1 outcome is allowed and is labelled a share.
  • Pooling rates. AVG or SUM over semanticType=rate, or a name matching rate|pct|percent|per_?\d+|proportion|ratio on a reference table, is refused unless it has the form SUM(rate*w)/SUM(w) with w the contract's weightColumn. The refusal shows that rewrite.
  • Overlapping categories.
  • Static: refuse a dim level literal in {'all','both','total','overall','any'} (case-insensitive) inside CASE or WHERE on a group column.
  • Contract and data: when a dimension's documented codebook, or its observed levels from the sampler, include such a level, the gate adds WHERE col NOT IN (<total levels>) and says so in the explanation, or holds when the user filtered on it explicitly. Example: CDC "All Sexes".
  • Runtime: when Σ__n > P_core, add the overlap line (4.3 d). The note reads "patients appear in more than one row; rows do not add up to the total".
  • Units.
  • +, -, comparison, COALESCE, GREATEST or UNION between columns with different contract units is refused unless one side is wrapped in the sandbox macro convert_unit(x, 'from', 'to'). The macro is defined from the P4 vocabulary's conversion table.
  • A literal threshold against a column outside [p01/10, p99*10] of observed values is held: "check units: <col> is recorded in <unit>". The percentiles are computed in the sandbox and never shown.
  • Each result column gets a unit:
    • AVG or MEDIAN(x) gets unit(x);
    • COUNT(DISTINCT pid) gets "patients";
    • COUNT(*) gets "visits", "events" or "rows" by grain;
    • a ratio gets "per ".
    • A column alias that says patients when it counts rows is held, using the same unit logic as query_service._unit_of.

docs.title: 6.1 Generation (sql/generate.py)
docs.text:
def generate(question: str, ctx: RenderedContext, examples: list[SqlExample], history: list[SqlTurn],
             client: OllamaClient, feedback: str | None) -> ModelOutput
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ModelOutput: sql: str | None; tool: ToolCall | None; raw_sha256: str
  • Request. Ollama /api/generate with format set to a JSON schema ({"sql": string|null, "tool": {...}|null}), temperature 0, num_ctx 8192, and the timeout llm_timeout_parse_s.
  • Examples. resources/config/sql_examples.yaml holds about 40 pairs of question and SQL over a toy patients/visits/labs/meds/micro schema. They cover top-N, rank, trend by year, percent change, pivot with count_if, rate per population, a 90-day window join, before/after, first-per-patient windows and follow-up edits. Three are retrieved by embedding similarity.
  • Repair. Up to 2 retries, feeding back the SqlRefusal text, following the _retry_with_dba_feedback_llm pattern.
  • 3B settings. maxJoins=1, a context budget of 2500 tokens, and SQL only (the tool calls come from routing, 6.4).
  • What a 7–8B model changes.
  • maxJoins=4, with time-window joins and follow-up edits enabled.
  • A 4000-token budget.
  • Tool calls in the same output.
  • Add ollama_sql_model to nl_query.yaml. Benchmark qwen2.5-coder:7b and qwen2.5-coder:3b against the llama models, since code-tuned models usually do better at SQL. The benchmark picks the default.

docs.title: 6.2 Plain-language plan (sql/explain.py)
docs.text:
explain(q: ValidatedQuery, contract) -> list[str] is deterministic, built from the AST and contract business names, never from model text. Example:

  1. "Start from microbiology results where the test is C. difficile toxin and the result is positive. Keep each patient's first positive test."
  2. "Join prescriptions on patient, for antibiotics started in the 90 days before that test."
  3. "Count distinct patients by year of the test. Groups under 11 patients are hidden."

It also lists the rewrites the gate added (total levels excluded, HAVING moved).

docs.title: 6.3 Editing and re-running
docs.text:
• QueryRequest adds:
  • mode: Literal["auto","intent","sql"] = "auto";
  • sql: str | None, a user-edited query that runs through the same validate_sql, gate and privacy steps with no model.
  • QueryResult adds answer_id: str, route: Literal["intent","sql","tool"] and sql: SqlPayload | None, where SqlPayload is {sql: canonical_sql, explanation: list[str], columns: list[ResultColumn], contract_ref: str}.
  • A new route POST /queries/sql/check returns validation and explanation without running anything, for live checking in the editor.
  • SSE adds sql_generated and sql_checked.
  • Holds reuse the confirm flow: plan_hash = sha256(canonical_sql + contract_ref + sorted(holds)).
  • A confirmation re-runs the stored plan (both paths, from step 3). The server keeps the plan it hashed, with what the plan was built against: the dataset version, the contract_ref and the layer's state_generation. On confirm, it runs that plan only if all three still match and the plan passes validation and the gate again. Otherwise it refuses: "The dataset or its description changed after you were asked to confirm. Ask the question again." A re-upload changes the version, and an accepted MetadataPatch, such as a column-choice synonym (§5.1), changes the contract_ref. It never re-parses the question. Today the question path re-parses, and the nondeterministic model tier can produce a different plan: covid_ms-or-012 was confirmed and then held again with "This plan is different from the one you approved" (core/execution_gate.py).
  • Electron gets a new electron/src/sqlPanel.js: a collapsible "How this was computed" with the explanation, the SQL in a textarea, and Run edited query.

docs.title: 6.4 Routing (core/query_service.py)
docs.text:
QueryService.ask runs the intent path first. That path is the fast one, and its golden suites show 0 WRONG. The new sql_fallback_eligible(result) -> bool is true when any of these hold: - parse failed; - confidence was below the threshold with no data hold; - the only hold is the word-accounting hold (unused_words_reason); - the plan was invalid because of an unsupported shape.

Data holds (grain, spellings, implausible values) never fall back, because only the user can settle them. Then SqlQueryService.ask_sql(...) runs (sql/service.py), with the same three-step locking pattern and state_generation re-check.

Step 4 is done when this fallback runs on one table and the questions that word accounting would hold are answered by model-written SQL. #106, which runs only user-typed SQL, does not finish step 4 on its own.

docs.title: 7. Statistics as tools (sql/tools.py)
docs.text:
ToolName = Literal["describe", "compare_groups", "find_predictors", "survival", "correlations"]
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ToolCall: tool: ToolName; cohort_sql: str; outcome: str | None; group: str | None
                predictors: tuple[str, ...] = (); time: str | None = None; event: str | None = None
  • cohort_sql is validated with validate_sql(..., allow_patient_rows=True). That is the only exception to "aggregated output": the frame never leaves the process.
  • It must be row_level or per_patient with __pid unique per row (checked at runtime), or it is held for grain.
  • It may have at most 12 columns, all named in the tool arguments.
  • The frame goes to an AnalysisContext (intent, primary, grouping, predictors, time, event variables). Then compute_analysis_by_type(df, context, entity_key="__pid"), with analysis["n_filtered_out"] = P_all − P_core so suppress_with_exclusions sees the complement. Then QueryService._with_findings (findings from ColumnUse), then present_analysis.
  • All of the existing floors, folding, OR/CI rendering and suppression apply unchanged.
  • In SQL, corr, regr_* and test-like constructs are refused with "use the statistics tool".
  • With 3B, the tool is picked by routing: an intent-path parse with intent COMPARE_GROUPS, FIND_PREDICTORS, SURVIVAL or CORRELATIONS whose cohort can't be expressed as filters. The model writes only cohort_sql. With 7–8B, the model can return the full ToolCall.

docs.title: 8. Follow-ups and conversation state
docs.text:
• SqlTurn: {question, route, canonical_sql, cohort_sql | None, columns: [name, kind, unit], contract_ref}. No result values. This is an invariant with a test: no prompt contains a number from a presented table. Domino Clinical Data Explorer enforces the same rule per tool.
  • Storage. In the session DB: add Message.payload_json with an Alembic migration (api/models/database.py). AsyncQueryService.conversation_history returns SqlTurns for the SQL route.
  • Prompt. The model sees the last 2 turns' question and SQL and is told to edit the SQL ("now by year", "only women").
  • "Those patients". The previous cohort_sql, or the core input of the last turn, is available as CTE previous_cohort. It is re-validated and recomputed, never cached results, so privacy is enforced again.
  • Contract changes. When contract_ref differs from the previous turn, the earlier SQL is re-validated against the new contract. A column that is now missing is refused with the reason.

docs.title: 9. Charts (sql/chart.py)
docs.text:
• choose_chart(columns: list[ResultColumn], rows) -> ChartSpec | None widens ChartSpec.type to bar|line|grouped_bar|heatmap. It is rule-based:
  • one temporal dim and 1–3 measures: line;
  • one categorical dim (at most MAX_GROUP_LEVELS) and one measure: bar;
  • two dims: grouped_bar, or heatmap when either has more than 6 levels;
  • otherwise a table.
  • A model chart hint is accepted only if it names result columns.
  • Data comes from presented rows only. Hidden cells are drawn as hatched gaps labelled "hidden (fewer than 11 patients)".
  • Histograms are core aggregates over floor(x/w)*w bins, so small bins are hidden.
  • Electron gets electron/src/chartView.js (inline SVG, no external library, which fits the CSP).
  • query_plan.generate_chart_spec moves here once both paths use it.

docs.title: 10. Lineage (P3) and methods export
docs.text:
• Events. lineage/events.py writes <data home>/lineage/<upload_id>/events.jsonl through storage/atomic.py append semantics. Event kinds:
  • upload;
  • contract_revision (change, ContractRef);
  • patch_decision;
  • declaration;
  • plan (run_key, plan_hash);
  • answer: {answer_id, route, contract_ref, product_ref, run_key|sql_sha256, canonical_sql, explanation, tool, model:{name, digest}, app_version, checks:{refusal, holds, notes}, suppression:{hidden_cells, folded}, presented_sha256}.
  • No patient values. SQL literals come from the question. The presented answer is stored only as a hash.
  • Index. lineage/index.py rebuilds <data home>/lineage/lineage.duckdb with tables nodes(id, kind, attrs JSON) and edges(src, dst, kind) from the JSONL. The JSONL is the source of truth.
  • Hooks:
  • UserDatasetStorage save (upload);
  • contracts/revisions.revise;
  • OverlayStore.accept_patch, reject_patch and revert;
  • QueryService._finish and SqlQueryService (answer).
  • Dataset deletion (storage/dataset_deletion.py) removes the lineage directory.
  • Methods export. lineage/methods.py::methods_markdown(answer_id) feeds GET /answers/{answer_id}/methods?format=md|json. Sections:
  • data source (dataset, version, contract version, source sha256);
  • cohort definition (explanation);
  • variables, with description, unit and concept taken from the contract at that contract_ref;
  • statistical methods (test names and CI method from the analysis payload);
  • the privacy rule applied;
  • software (app, DuckDB, statsmodels, lifelines, model and digest);
  • the SQL appendix.

docs.title: 11.1 Corpus
docs.text:
src/clinical_analytics/eval/corpus/corpus.yaml lists each dataset's id, url, sha256, license, dictionary_url, prepare (a function name) and tables. The data is fetched to <data home>/bench/ by make bench-corpus-fetch and is never committed (check_no_data_files.py). Datasets:

  • COVID-MS GDSI public sample. Patient grain, with coded columns and a dictionary.
  • PhysioNet Sepsis 2019. Training set A, CC-BY 4.0. Hourly PSV files are joined into one long table with patient_id taken from the file name; this is the visit/hour grain test.
  • MIMIC-III demo and MIMIC-IV demo (ODbL). Multi-table ZIP: patients, admissions, prescriptions, microbiologyevents, labevents, d_labitems. These test joins and time windows, including the C. diff question. Because there are 100 patients, many answers must be HELD, which tests privacy.
  • UCI Diabetes 130-US hospitals. Encounter grain, readmission and rates.
  • UCI Heart Disease (Cleveland). Coded categoricals, for the means-of-codes guard.
  • A CDC state-year table with All Sexes and All Ages rows, and a rate per 100k with population. For example, NCHS provisional COVID-19 deaths by sex, age and state. It tests overlapping categories and pooling. Pin the exact table in the manifest.

docs.title: 11.2 Questions and oracles
docs.text:
• Questions live in tests/eval/corpus/questions/<dataset>.yaml. Each has {id, question, capability, follow_up_of?, expect: answer|held, confirm: bool}. There are about 300 across these capabilities:
  • count, describe, top-N, rank;
  • trend by year, percent change, pivot, rate per population;
  • time-window join, window function, before/after;
  • follow-up chain, statistics tool, arbitrary aggregate;
  • guard probes (grain, overlap, units, pooling, codes);
  • privacy probes: listings, HAVING tricks, LAG next to small cells, complements of a CTE, identifier literals, read_parquet and COPY injection in the question text;
  • unenforceable patterns, with expect: held.
  • Oracles are tests/eval/corpus/oracles/<dataset>.py: Polars only, written without reading the app's SQL. Each returns OracleAnswer(frame, unit, cell_patients: dict[CellKey, int]), so the scorer knows which cells must be hidden.

docs.title: 11.3 Harness and scoring
docs.text:
• eval/corpus/run.py (make bench-sql MODEL=llama3.2:3b). Each run:
  • sets a fresh CLINICAL_ANALYTICS_DATA_HOME temporary directory and starts a fresh API process (TestClient on api.main), so there are no layer caches, prompt-learning overlays or declarations;
  • uploads every dataset through POST /datasets/upload, the real staging path;
  • asks each question chain in a new session;
  • when confirm: true, confirms holds the way eval/headless.ask(confirm=True) does.
  • Grading reads the presented answer (presented_answer-style), never raw frames:
  • RIGHT: every shown value matches the oracle (counts exact; statistics within 1e-4 relative), labels and unit match, and every oracle cell of 1–10 patients is hidden. Secondary hidden cells are allowed. An expect: held question that is held counts as RIGHT.
  • WRONG: a shown value differs, the unit or grain is wrong, a non-hidden oracle row is missing, an expect: held question is answered, or there is a LEAK (a shown cell with 1–10 oracle patients, or a small level's label).
  • HELD: held or refused with a reason when expect: answer.
  • ERROR: exception, timeout, model unavailable, or validation failed after retries.
  • Each question runs 3 times at temperature 0 to show nondeterminism. A WRONG in any run counts.
  • Two rates, never added together (from step 3). RIGHT mixes usefulness with safety, because a correctly held expect: held question is RIGHT (eval/corpus/score.py). The harness therefore reports:
  • answered right ÷ questions with expect: answer, the usefulness rate (COVID-MS baseline: 1 of 14);
  • correctly held ÷ questions with expect: held;
  • right after one clarification, for a confirm: true question answered after one column choice (§5.1);
  • unsafe = WRONG ÷ all questions, which must be 0. A LEAK is graded WRONG and flagged, so it is counted once, inside WRONG.

The CI gate runs make accept DATASET=covid_ms MODEL=none, the pattern and embedding tiers without a model, and gates on its answered-right count against a baseline stored in the repository, not on RIGHT. That count measures the question path without the model. The run with the model is the manual release gate below. - Held-out questions. Each corpus dataset gets a permanent tests/eval/corpus/questions/<dataset>.heldout.yaml: about 15 paraphrases of the same intents, written by someone who has not read the code, graded by the same oracles. Dev and held-out results are reported separately, and only held-out results count toward a step's "done". Fixes are never tuned on the held-out file. The COVID-MS file lands on main and is scored there, with and without the model, before #107 merges; that run is the baseline step 3's "rises" is measured against. - Issues. Each reproducible WRONG, LEAK, ERROR or unacceptable HOLD has a GitHub issue per cause (see Merge gate). Question YAML gains issue: and fixed_by: keys, so a regression names its issue and PR. - The run records the model digest, not only its name. - Ship bar: - 0 WRONG (including 0 LEAK) for both the 3B model and the chosen 7–8B model; - no answered-right regressions on the intent-expressible subset compared with the intent path alone; - the answered-right rate reported per capability, on held-out questions. - CI. The privacy and validator adversarial suites run on the synthetic fixtures (tests/sql/), and the MODEL=none acceptance run gates as above. The full benchmark with the model is a manual, release-gate job because it needs Ollama.

docs.title: Coexistence
docs.text:
• The intent path stays the first route.
  • The SQL path is behind sql_path.enabled in nl_query.yaml, default false until PR 8 meets the ship bar.
  • Both paths go through contracts/gate.py and both write lineage.

docs.title: What to delete, and when
docs.text:
• Immediately, in PR 1:
  • resources/config/ollama.yaml, which is reference only and not read;
  • the stats min/max/top_values and _reconstruct_inferred_schema_from_semantic_layer in autocontext.py.
  • After the ship bar, when SQL RIGHT is at least Tier-3 RIGHT on the corpus:
  • Tier 3 LLM intent parsing: NLQueryEngine._llm_parse, _build_llm_prompt, _extract_query_intent_from_llm_response, _dba_validate_llm and _retry_with_dba_feedback_llm;
  • core/autocontext.py, with callers moved to contracts/context.py;
  • query_plan.generate_chart_spec.
  • Keep: Tier 1/2 and QueryPlan, which are deterministic and fast.
  • Docs: mark docs/vision/UNIFIED_VISION.md superseded by ADR013, and update AS_BUILT_ARCHITECTURE.md's known-limits section.

docs.title: PRs
docs.text:
The steel thread sets the order, and only the step being worked on is built. Revised 2026-11-14:

  • Step 3 is PR 1 as #107 builds it, plus the alias step and the column-choice hold moved forward from PR 2 (§1.4, §5.1), plus confirmation replay (§6.3). The merge order is in Purpose, step 3.
  • Step 4 is PR 5 in #106's smaller form (§2.1), PR 6 on one table, and the per-answer filter check and step-by-step count (§4.5).

  • Waiting: PR 2's review UI and revisions, PR 3 (lineage), PR 9 (charts), §1.5 (ODPS) and packaging. None of them moves the acceptance table now.

  • Contract enriched from documentation and metadata patches; AutoContext built from the contract. This is the smallest useful PR.

  • Content:
    • per-table schema objects;
    • dictionary entries turned into MetadataPatch(provenance="dictionary"), auto-accepted on exact name match;
    • accepted patches and declarations folded in;
    • contracts/revisions.py;
    • contracts/context.py::render_context and SafeSampler running on the layer connection, before the sandbox exists;
    • build_autocontext as an adapter;
    • the privacy fix to the context stats;
    • eval/corpus/{corpus.yaml,fetch.py} and a context benchmark.
  • The context benchmark measures, per corpus dataset:
    • (a) upload and render succeed, with no crash;
    • (b) description coverage and (c) unit and codebook precision and recall, against the dataset's own data dictionary;
    • (d) zero rendered levels below 11 patients, checked by an oracle;
    • (e) the token budget is respected;
    • (f) golden and hard-question suites don't regress;
    • (g) Tier-3 RIGHT, WRONG, HELD and ERROR on intent-expressible corpus questions, before and after.
  • Contract review UI and revisions in the ADR011 flow; P4 vocabulary. SET_CONCEPT, the curated LOINC subset under resources/vocabulary/ with a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry, and unit conversion data. (Contract synonyms into _build_alias_index moved to step 3.)
  • Lineage P3. JSONL, the DuckDB index, answer_id and contract_ref on QueryResult, and the methods export, for the intent path first.
  • P5 gate on the intent path, and the ODPS product file. check_plan runs in _finish. The ColumnUse and ViewStats refactor of answer_checks, with behaviour unchanged and the golden suites as proof.
  • SQL sandbox, validator, privacy rewrite and suppression, with user-typed SQL only. Behind a flag, with POST /queries/sql/check and the SQL panel. Includes the adversarial privacy suite and the engine-level escape tests. This is #106, in the scope of §2.1. The per-answer check (§4.5) lands on this path before the flag can be on by default.
  • Model-written SQL. Generation, examples, repair, explain.py, routing fallback, and the confirm flow for SQL holds. With the per-answer filter check and step-by-step count (§4.5), this finishes step 4.
  • Statistics tools (sql/tools.py).
  • Follow-ups and conversation state, plus the full capability benchmark run and the ship decision for 3B and 7–8B.
  • Charts (sql/chart.py, chartView.js).
  • Deletions listed above, and ADR013 marked Accepted.
  • Later. A dataset-version log of shown counts against differencing across questions, at step 6 (§4.4), and GROUPING SETS with explicit overlap lines.

docs.title: Critical Files for Implementation
docs.text:
• contracts/builder.py
  • core/autocontext.py
  • core/result_presentation.py
  • core/answer_checks.py
  • core/query_service.py

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
Review Date: 2025-12-27 Platform: Clinical Analytics Platform Total LOC: ~13,000 across 46 Python files Overall Grade: B+ (85/100)

This comprehensive review identifies 37 critical findings across 8 dimensions: code quality, security, performance, architecture, data integrity, patterns, agent accessibility, and complexity. The platform has excellent architectural foundations but requires immediate attention to security vulnerabilities, Pandas usage violations, and error handling patterns.

docs.title: Critical Issues Summary
docs.text:
• 🔴 CRITICAL (P1): 15 findings - MUST fix before production
  • 🟡 IMPORTANT (P2): 14 findings - Should fix this sprint
  • 🔵 NICE-TO-HAVE (P3): 8 findings - Backlog items

docs.title: 1. Code Quality Review (Grade: B-)
docs.text:
Strengths: - Modern Python patterns (dataclasses, type hints, pathlib) - Good architecture (registry, semantic layer, config-driven) - Polars usage in core modules - Well-documented complex logic

Critical Issues:

docs.title: 1.1 Pandas Usage Violations (P1)
docs.text:
Files: 26 files import Pandas despite project mandate for "Polars only" - analysis/stats.py - ENTIRE file uses Pandas - analysis/survival.py - ENTIRE file uses Pandas - core/semantic.py - Returns pd.DataFrame instead of pl.DataFrame - core/profiling.py - Converts Polars to Pandas

Impact: 2-5x memory overhead, violates project standards Action: Migrate to Polars or add explicit justification comments

docs.title: 1.2 Missing Type Hints (P1)
docs.text:
Files: 12+ functions missing return types - multi_table_handler.py:23 - Missing cls type annotation - semantic.py:300 - Missing view parameter type - stats.py:7-11 - Uses Any instead of specific model type

Impact: Reduced type safety, harder to maintain Action: Add type hints to all functions, target 100% coverage

docs.title: 1.3 Error Handling Anti-Patterns (P1)
docs.text:
Pattern: 8 bare except: clauses, 30+ broad except Exception

Examples: 

# variable_detector.py:85
except:  # ❌ SILENT FAILURE
    pass

# nl_query_engine.py:351
except Exception as e:  # ❌ TOO BROAD
    print(f"Failed: {e}")  # ❌ print() instead of logger
    pass

Impact: Silent failures, debugging nightmares Action: Replace with specific exceptions, remove pass

docs.title: 2. Security Audit (Grade: 0/10 - CRITICAL)
docs.text: OVERALL RISK LEVEL: CRITICAL - DO NOT DEPLOY WITH PHI

docs.title: 2.1 No Authentication/Authorization (P1)
docs.text:
Status: ❌ COMPLETELY MISSING

Impact: - Anyone with network access can view ALL patient data - No audit trail of data access - HIPAA compliance impossible

Action: Implement Streamlit authentication + RBAC before ANY production deployment

docs.title: 2.2 SQL Injection Vulnerability (P1)
docs.text:
File: semantic.py:202-205

# VULNERABLE:
duckdb_con.execute(
    f"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE {table_name} AS SELECT * FROM read_csv_auto(?)",
    [abs_path]
)

Attack Vector: Malicious dataset name like "; DROP TABLE patients; --" Action: Use quoted identifiers: f'"{table_name}"'

docs.title: 2.3 Path Traversal Vulnerability (P1)
docs.text:
File: user_datasets.py:391-431

Issue: ZIP extraction without path validation allows ../../../etc/passwd.csv Action: Implement safe_extract() with path validation

docs.title: 2.4 No PHI/PII Encryption (P1)
docs.text:
Status: All uploaded files stored in PLAINTEXT

HIPAA Violations: - ❌ No encryption at rest (164.312(a)(2)(iv)) - ❌ No access controls (164.308(a)(3)) - ❌ No audit logs (164.312(b))

Action: Implement Fernet encryption for all uploads

docs.title: 2.5 XSS Vulnerabilities (P2)
docs.text:
Files: question_engine.py:388, app.py:228-229

Issue: User input displayed without HTML escaping Action: Use html.escape() for all user-controlled strings

docs.title: 3. Performance Analysis (Grade: C+)
docs.text: Critical Performance Issues:

docs.title: 3.1 Pandas Performance Overhead (P1)
docs.text:
Impact: 2-5x memory usage, 5-30x slower aggregations Files: 26 files use Pandas

Action: Migrate stats.py and profiling.py to Polars

docs.title: Consolidate Documentation & Implement Question-Driven Semantic Analysis
docs.text: Status: Phase 1 & 2 Complete ✅ Priority: P0 (Critical - addresses core user friction) Created: 2025-12-24 Updated: 2025-12-24 Owner: Development Team PR: #2 - Phase 1+2: Documentation Infrastructure & Natural Language Query Engine

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
This plan addresses the critical transition from hardcoded, menu-driven analysis to an intelligent, question-driven semantic analysis system. Based on comprehensive research of repository documentation (28 files, 11,500 lines) and modern NL query best practices, this plan consolidates documentation infrastructure while implementing a natural language interface that transforms clinical analytics from "click through menus" to "just ask your question."

Key Outcomes: 1. ✅ Documentation infrastructure with MkDocs + Material (auto-generated API docs, single source of truth) - COMPLETE 2. ✅ Natural language query engine (free-form text → semantic understanding → dynamic SQL) - COMPLETE 3. ⏳ Automatic schema inference (zero manual configuration for any dataset) - PENDING (Phase 3) 4. ⏳ Multi-table support for complex datasets like MIMIC-IV - PENDING (Phase 4)

docs.title: ✅ Phase 1: Documentation Infrastructure (Complete - 2025-12-24)
docs.text:
Delivered: - MkDocs + Material theme with auto-generated API docs - 23 comprehensive documentation pages (~11,500 lines) - GitHub Actions workflow for auto-deployment - Complete restructuring of docs/ directory

Key Files: - mkdocs.yml - Site configuration - docs/index.md - Homepage - docs/getting-started/ - Installation, Quick Start, Data Upload - docs/user-guide/ - Question-driven analysis, Statistical tests, Interpreting results - docs/architecture/ - System design documentation - docs/api-reference/ - Auto-generated API docs - docs/development/ - Contributing, Setup, Testing - .github/workflows/docs.yml - Auto-deploy to GitHub Pages

Commits: - 58dec2b - docs: reorganize documentation structure - a3f45b2 - feat(docs): implement Phase 1 documentation infrastructure with MkDocs

docs.title: ✅ Phase 2: Natural Language Query Engine (Complete - 2025-12-24)
docs.text:
Delivered: - Three-tier NL query parsing engine (regex → embeddings → LLM) - Full UI integration with confidence display - 15 query templates covering all analysis types - Fuzzy variable matching with synonyms - Bidirectional switching (NL ↔ structured questions)

Key Files: - src/clinical_analytics/core/nl_query_engine.py - Core NL parsing engine - QueryIntent dataclass - NLQueryEngine class with three-tier architecture - Pattern matching, semantic embeddings, LLM fallback - src/clinical_analytics/ui/components/question_engine.py - UI integration - ask_free_form_question() method - Confidence display and interpretation - src/clinical_analytics/ui/pages/7_🔬_Analyze.py - Unified analysis page - Defaults to free-form NL query - Fallback to structured questions

Technical Details: - Tier 1: Regex (90-95% confidence, <1ms latency) - Tier 2: Semantic embeddings via sentence-transformers (70-90% confidence, ~50ms) - Tier 3: LLM fallback stub (triggers clarifying questions) - Privacy-preserving: Tiers 1 & 2 fully local (no API calls)

Dependencies Added: - sentence-transformers ^5.2.0 - scikit-learn ^1.8.0 - seaborn ^0.13.2 - torch ^2.9.1

Commits: - dcb85cd - feat(nl-query): implement Phase 2 natural language query engine core - f61d201 - feat(ui): integrate NL query engine with Streamlit UI - aaf18f5 - fix(deps): add missing seaborn dependency

Example Queries: - "compare survival by treatment arm" - "what predicts mortality" - "descriptive statistics" - "correlation between age and outcome"

docs.title: 🔄 Phase 3: Automatic Schema Inference (In Progress)
docs.text:
Delivered Features: - ✅ Remove all hardcoded YAML configs - ✅ Auto-detect patient IDs, outcomes, time variables from DataFrame - ✅ Parse data dictionary PDFs using LangChain (NEW!) - ✅ Merge PDF metadata with inferred schema (NEW!) - ✅ Schema inference for uploaded datasets - ✅ Consistent handling of built-in and uploaded datasets

Key Innovation: Dictionary-Enhanced Schema Inference Before users see their data, the system now: 1. Uses the data dictionary the user supplied with their upload (ZIP contents or a standalone PDF; none ship in the repo) 2. Extracts column descriptions, types, and valid values using LangChain 3. Merges PDF metadata with DataFrame-based inference 4. Presents enriched schema with both statistical analysis + documentation context 5. Boosts confidence scores when dictionary confirms inferred types

Implementation: - schema_inference.py: - DictionaryMetadata dataclass for PDF-extracted info - parse_dictionary_pdf() using LangChain's PyPDFLoader - infer_schema_with_dictionary() merges both sources - registry.py: - register_from_dataframe() with automatic schema inference - Stores DataFrames for auto-inferred datasets

Dependencies Added: - langchain ^1.2.0 - langchain-community ^0.4.1

Target: PR #3 (in progress)

docs.title: ⏸️ Phase 4: Multi-Table Support (DEFERRED_TO_V2)
docs.text:
Status Update (2025-12-27): This phase is deferred to V2 pending completion of the Cohort-First Single Table MVP. The strategic decision was made to prioritize "Doctor uploads CSV, it works in 5 minutes" over multi-table complexity.

Completed Infrastructure (preserved for V2): - ✅ ZIP upload with multiple CSVs - ✅ Auto-detect foreign key relationships using Polars/DuckDB - ✅ Build join graph and execute joins via DuckDB SQL - ⏸️ MIMIC-IV-style dataset support - deferred - ⏸️ Unified cohort creation from related tables - deferred (OOM issues to resolve)

Implementation (gated by MULTI_TABLE_ENABLED feature flag): - multi_table_handler.py: - TableRelationship dataclass for FK detection - MultiTableHandler with DuckDB-based joins - Primary/foreign key detection via cardinality + naming patterns - BFS join graph traversal - user_datasets.py: - save_zip_upload() method for multi-table ZIP files (disabled in V1) - Automatic relationship detection and cohort building - Metadata includes table counts and join relationships - src/clinical_analytics/ui/config.py: - MULTI_TABLE_ENABLED feature flag (default: false)

Blocking Issues for V2: - OutOfMemory (OOM) with large tables (chartevents 668k rows) - Aggregate-before-join architecture needed (see .cursor/plans/multi-table_handler_refactor*.md)

Target: V2 after single-table MVP is validated

docs.text:

docs.title: Current Pain Points
docs.text:
1. Hardcoded Analysis Pages - 7 separate UI pages (Descriptive Stats, Compare Groups, Risk Factors, Survival, Correlations, etc.) - Each requires user to explicitly choose analysis type - Duplicate dataset loading code across pages - Menu-driven navigation creates cognitive overhead

User Feedback: "this feels very hardcoded? I want the analysis to be driven by questions by the user"

2. Manual Schema Configuration - Built-in datasets (COVID-MS, Sepsis, MIMIC-III) require handwritten YAML configs - New datasets need manual mapping of patient IDs, outcomes, time variables - Inconsistent between built-in (YAML) and uploaded (auto-detected) datasets

User Feedback: "infer schema, don't hardcode"

3. Structured Questions vs Free-Form Queries - Current QuestionEngine uses radio buttons for intent classification - Users must fit their question into predefined categories - No support for natural language like "show me survival by treatment arm"

User Feedback: Highlighted gap between current structured questions vs desired NL queries in research/NL_QUERY_BEST_PRACTICES.md

4. Documentation Fragmentation - 28 markdown files (~11,500 lines) across multiple directories - No centralized API documentation - Specs scattered in docs/specs/, historical plans in root - No automated docs site generation

User Feedback: "/workflows:plan docs/README.md as a part of the plan consolidate documentation"

docs.title: Documentation Best Practices (2025)
docs.text:
Tool Recommendation: MkDocs + Material theme + mkdocstrings

Rationale: - Lightweight setup: No Sphinx complexity, just markdown - Modern aesthetics: Material Design, mobile-responsive, dark mode - Auto-generated API docs: mkdocstrings extracts from type hints - SSOT principle: Single source of truth from code comments - CI/CD friendly: GitHub Actions → GitHub Pages in 5 minutes

Industry Examples: - FastAPI uses MkDocs + Material (excellent UX) - Pydantic uses mkdocs-material with auto-generated reference - Typer documentation is clean, searchable, versioned

docs.title: Natural Language Query Architecture
docs.text:
Research Source: docs/research/NL_QUERY_BEST_PRACTICES.md (2,794 lines)

Key Findings: 1. Modern Approach: LLM-based semantic understanding + RAG with semantic layers 2. Error Reduction: Semantic layers reduce SQL errors by ~66% when combined with RAG 3. Accuracy: Transformer models (BERT, RoBERTa) achieve 85%+ accuracy for intent classification 4. Three-Tier Pattern: Pattern matching → Semantic embeddings → LLM fallback 5. Privacy: sentence-transformers enables local embeddings (no PHI exposure to APIs)

Recommended Architecture:

User Query (text)
    ↓
[Tier 1] Pattern Matching (regex for common patterns)
    ↓ (if no match)
[Tier 2] Semantic Embeddings (sentence-transformers)
    ↓ (retrieve top-k similar queries/intents)
[Tier 3] LLM Fallback (structured prompt with semantic layer metadata)
    ↓
Intent + Variables Extracted
    ↓
Semantic Layer (Ibis SQL generation)
    ↓
Results + Plain Language Interpretation
